Further, we developed four machine learning models to predict evacuation time, among which the Improved Particle Swarm Optimization-integrated Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (IPSOCNN-LSTM) model achieved superior predictive accuracy. The results confirm the efficacy of the proposed framework in identifying critical evacuation risks and supporting real-time emergency decision-making. This research contributes a scientifically grounded, data-driven paradigm for dynamic risk assessment in built environments and offers scalable solutions for enhancing safety in aging urban infrastructure under various emergency scenarios.

title: Early warning and prevention of mud cakes in large-diameter slurry shields: Insights from construction parameter data analysis and interpretable machine learning
abstract: Mud cake blockage in large-diameter slurry shield (LDSS) construction is one of the key factors affecting the high efficiency and quality of tunnel construction. To address the lack of intelligent methods for mud cake detection, an early warning interpretable machine learning approach based on Exponential-Trigonometric Optimization (ETO)-Natural gradient boosting (NGBoost)- Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) for LDSS is proposed. Twenty-four types of construction-related parameter data for LDSSs are selected as input indicators. The knowledge-driven method is used to analyse the construction parameters to obtain the risk level of the mud cake, and the degree of mud cake formation is classified via the ETO-NGBoost intelligent algorithm. The results are as follows: (1) ETO-NGBoost can obtain mud cake supervised classification results with high precision and high generalization performance, and the precision, recall and F1 score values in the test set are all above 0.93. (2) SHAP improves the interpretability and determines the important factors of slurry shields that influence the formation of mud cakes. (3) The supervised classification model driven by knowledge and data can be used to build a mud cake detection and early warning framework to judge the degree of mud cake formation in time. On this basis, effective prevention and control measures can be taken.
keywords: Dual-driven knowledge and construction parameter data

title: Fed-Joint: Joint modeling of nonlinear degradation signals and failure events for remaining useful life prediction using federated learning
abstract: Many failure mechanisms of machinery are closely related to the behavior of condition monitoring (CM) signals. To achieve a cost-effective preventive maintenance strategy, accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction based on the signals is of paramount importance. However, the CM signals are often recorded at different factories and production lines, with limited amounts of data. Unfortunately, these datasets have rarely been shared between the sites due to data confidentiality and ownership issues, a lack of computing and storage power, and high communication costs associated with data transfer between sites and a data center. Another challenge in real applications is that the CM signals are often not explicitly specified \textit{a priori}, meaning that existing methods, which often usually a parametric form, may not be applicable. To address these challenges, we propose a new prognostic framework for RUL prediction using the joint modeling of nonlinear degradation signals and time-to-failure data within a federated learning scheme. The proposed method constructs a nonparametric degradation model using a federated multi-output Gaussian process and then employs a federated survival model to predict failure times and probabilities for in-service machinery. The superiority of the proposed method over other alternatives is demonstrated through comprehensive simulation studies and a case study using turbofan engine degradation signal data that include run-to-failure events.

title: An anomaly detection method for gas turbines in power plants using conditional variational autoencoder optimized with self-attention
abstract: An innovative anomaly detection (AD) framework designed for gas turbines (GTs) in power plants working under variable operating conditions (OCs) was proposed based on conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) optimized with self-attention (SA) in this paper. Three key factors contribute to the model's superior performance in AD. First, the marginal distributions (MDs) of parameters were transformed into conditional probability distributions (CPDs) by incorporating OC variables as conditional inputs in the variational autoencoder (VAE) model, and decoupled modeling of equipment states and external OCs is achieved. Second, by embedding SA modules, the method dynamically adjusts weight allocation of the parameters to capture complex dependencies among them, which can enhance the capability of the model to represent intricate coupling relationships in multi-dimensional parameters. Third, the logarithmic reconstruction probability (LRP), derived from the probabilistic output of SA-CVAE, serves as a unified health indicator (HI) to evaluate the health condition of the GT. The indicator not only accounts for the discrepancy between the reconstructed and original inputs but also incorporates the influence of latent variable (LV) variance on the reconstruction results. Experiments were carried out on one synthetic, one public, and two real-world datasets, with SA-CVAE compared against six leading AD methods. The results demonstrate that under varying OCs, SA-CVAE exhibits superior performance in AD tasks, achieving leading or competitive results across key evaluation metrics.

title: Confidence interval-based robust topology optimization with active learning
abstract: Robust topology optimization (RTO) designs material distribution to improve structural performance while reducing its sensitivity to uncertainties. However, for classical probabilistic RTO, it remains challenging to achieve a trade-off between efficiency and applicability to problems involving complex multi-source uncertainties. To address this difficulty, a confidence interval-based RTO (CI-RTO) method is proposed in this paper, which simultaneously improves the structural response and its robustness through minimizing a weighted sum of the median and the width of the confidence interval. The method integrates Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) and the Kriging model to estimate the objective function. Inheriting non-intrusiveness from MCS and imposing no restrictions on input uncertainties, CI-RTO is capable of addressing complex multi-source uncertainties and non-linear relationships between response and random variables. Meanwhile, the Kriging model alleviates the computational burden arising from large-scale sampling, and a confidence interval active learning (CIAL) strategy is developed for its efficient construction. By adaptively improving modeling accuracy around the median and confidence bounds, CIAL significantly reduces the training cost of the Kriging model, thereby further accelerating CI-RTO. In addition, regarding sensitivity analysis, CI-RTO holds a natural advantage over classical RTO methods that minimize mean and standard deviation, since its computational cost is merely three times that of deterministic topology optimization (DTO). The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using four numerical examples, including macro, micro, and 3D design problems, where multiple uncertainties and non-linear responses to uncertain parameters are incorporated. Comparisons with other methods confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of CI-RTO.

title: Estimating node importance in transportation networks: A scalable machine learning approach
abstract: Urban transportation networks are vulnerable to performance degradation from node-level congestion, such as accidents or capacity overloads. Traditional vulnerability analyses employ iterative traffic assignment to quantify the impact of each congested node on total travel time (TTT). Although accurate, this process results in substantial computational costs and becomes prohibitively slow for large or dynamic networks. To address these limitations, we develop a scalable machine learning framework that predicts the TTT impact of individual node failures. Our model uses features drawn from origin–destination demand data, link attributes, network centrality measures, and socio-economic contexts. We construct an ensemble of four base learners — Random Forests, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Support Vector Classifier — combined via Logistic Regression as a meta-learner to classify nodes into high, medium, and low importance categories, and include a Multi-Layer Perceptron model for comparison. Evaluation across six real-world transportation networks demonstrates that our approach consistently achieves up to 85% classification accuracy while reducing computation time by up to 94%. We enhance interpretability through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), which identify initial link flow estimates as the most influential predictor. Furthermore, we verify model transferability by training on small variants of the Berlin and Birmingham networks and successfully applying the same models to their full-scale networks and two additional transportation networks. Our results confirm that the proposed framework offers rapid and reliable identification of critical intersections, facilitating more efficient network planning and resilience assessment.

title: A reinforcement learning approach to network-level maintenance planning of co-located road and water infrastructures with interdependencies
abstract: Due to co-location and spatial proximity, deteriorating transportation infrastructure (TI) and water infrastructure (WI) are geographically interdependent, exhibiting complex interactions both within and across systems. Failures from degradation or maintenance disruptions in one system can impair its own performance and cascade into the other. However, many existing studies address long-term maintenance only at the component, subsystem, or single-system level, without fully accounting for interdependencies both within and across co-located infrastructures. This paper proposes a network-wide joint long-term maintenance planning framework that integrates traffic and hydraulic simulations to capture interdependencies within and across multiple infrastructure systems. A reinforcement learning-based optimization model is formulated to minimize the expected cumulative costs of co-located TI and WI systems over a long-term planning horizon while accounting for future uncertainties in the deterioration of roads and pipes. The model jointly quantifies both short-term and long-term economic impacts of joint maintenance decisions at network level by comprehensively investigating diverse topological relationships and interactions between co-located roads and pipes. The framework is further validated through a realistic case study in Ybor City, Tampa, and benchmarked against alternative maintenance strategies, demonstrating cost savings achieved through proactive, coordinated decision-making across interdependent TI and WI systems.

title: Multi-modal graph convolutional network for vessel trajectory prediction based on cooperative intention enhance using conditional variational autoencoder
abstract: Advances in maritime instrumentation and measurement (I&M), particularly through the widespread adoption of automatic identification system (AIS), have significantly accelerated the development of intelligent situational awareness systems (ISAS). As a critical component of ISAS, cooperative navigation demands greater accuracy and reliability in vessel trajectory prediction. Nevertheless, challenges arising from complex inter-vessel interactions and implicit intention inference expose limitations in modeling explicit and implicit relationships and ensuring the robustness of trajectory prediction. To address these challenges, we propose a cooperative intention enhance multi-modal graph convolutional network (CIE-MGCN) to learn and predict the future vessel trajectories. The CIE-MGCN is composed of three primary components: Interaction Extractor, Intention Constructor, and Trajectory Generator. In Interaction Extractor, we designed the social-community extractor (SCE) to construct diverse interaction graphs that capture both cooperative and adversarial relationships among vessel trajectories, and the multi-modal transformer (MMT) to fuse explicit interaction features across various modalities. In Intention Constructor, we introduce a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE)-based approach to infer implicit relationships and capture potential future behavioral variations and multi-modal probability distributions of future trajectories are produced by Trajectory Generator. Extensive experiments on real-world navigation data show that CIE-MGCN outperforms state-of-the-art models in accuracy and robustness, owing to its strong reasoning and learning capabilities. These reliable predictions further support cooperative navigation within ISAS by enhancing coordination and decision-making among multi-vessel.

title: Contrastive decoupling graph neural network with deviation-diffusivity cooperative node selector for equipment remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have been widely applied to remaining useful life (RUL) prediction driven by multi-source information fusion. However, the conventional GNN-based approaches use the shared node features for both RUL prediction and spatial dependency modeling, which may induce implicit information conflicts. Moreover, they have no effective mechanisms for identifying the weakly correlated nodes, which causes the prediction accuracy to be easily disturbed by noise. To resolve potential information conflicts, we propose a novel node feature contrastive decoupling module (NFCDM). The NFCDM employs a cross-fusion-contrastive decoupling strategy to explicitly decompose node features into global degradation features for RUL prediction and local relational features for spatial dependency modeling. Task-specific contrastive decoupling constraints are further designed to ensure the task relevance and information independence of the decoupled features. In addition, to achieve the effective node screening, a deviation-diffusivity cooperative node selector (DDCS) is proposed. This novel selector is capable of constructing joint evaluation metrics based on the deviation of global degradation features and the information diffusion capability of nodes to adaptively discard redundant nodes. Built upon these two novel modules, the contrastive decoupling graph neural network with deviation-diffusivity cooperative node selector (CDGNN-DDCS) is proposed for RUL prediction. Comparative experiments on public datasets confirm the superiority of the proposed method. Lastly, its engineering practicality is successfully verified via an RUL prediction experiment on actual wind turbines.

title: An efficient graph neural networks surrogate model for slope reliability analysis considering soil spatial variability
abstract: Soil spatial variability significantly affects slope stability and landslide behaviors, particularly under complex geological conditions where traditional finite element analysis (FEA), while precise, incurs prohibitive computational costs. This study introduces a new surrogate model leveraging graph attention networks (GAT) equipped with sample and aggregate (SAGE) sampling, designed to efficiently handle large-scale data while predicting slope safety factors and identifying potential slip surfaces. The GAT model utilizes a spatial graph construction based on k-dimensional trees (KD-Trees), enabling the effective representation of complex mechanical interactions within the soil. The results indicate the superior performance of this model over traditional machine learning methods such as random forest, feedforward neural networks, support vector regression, and convolutional neural networks, achieving a mean squared error of 0.000218 and an R2 of 0.995. The application of GAT with SAGE sampling highlights the potential of graph neural networks to significantly enhance real-time slope stability monitoring and risk assessment in the geotechnical engineering field, demonstrating a promising direction for computationally efficient surrogate modeling.

title: Reverse Variational Autoencoder: A probabilistic inference framework for structural health monitoring and inverse analysis in engineering
abstract: Inverse analysis in structural engineering involves inferring uncertain parameters from limited external observations, which is crucial for structural health monitoring and maintenance. However, real-world applications often face under-constrained problems with multiple possible solutions due to sparse measurements. This study proposes a Bayesian deep learning-based framework, termed Reverse Variational Auto-Encoder (RVAE), to fulfill efficient probabilistic structural inverse analysis. The RVAE framework modifies the original VAE structure to consider the causality relationship underlying inverse problems, enabling a semi-supervised learning paradigm for label-agnostic scenarios. The effectiveness of the RVAE framework is validated through a grid structure experiment. The implemented model successfully reveals all possible solutions for bending amplitudes, strains, and node displacements, with root-mean-squared reconstruction errors of 1.21 %, 2.77 %, and 1.36 %, respectively. A comparative analysis is conducted between mainstream inversion algorithms and RVAE. The results demonstrate that while all the other inversion algorithms achieve low reconstruction errors, they provide single-solution estimation, thus highlighting RVAE's capability to provide the most comprehensive information. RVAE's capability for real-time probabilistic estimation of structural parameters is further discussed and demonstrated in a full-scale bridge tower experiment, where it utilizes multi-sensor data to infer critical structural parameters, showing strong adaptability to noisy, incomplete, and heterogeneous monitoring inputs. In summary, RVAE tackles the challenges of large-scale parameter inversion in engineering structures by enabling efficient probabilistic inference under sparse observations. It supports semi-supervised learning in label-agnostic scenarios and real-time prediction of multiple plausible solutions, thereby fulfilling the synchronous updating requirements of digital twin systems.

title: Explainable artificial intelligence based intelligent fault diagnosis: A systematic review from applications to insights
abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD) has become a key enabler for condition-based maintenance, yet its “black-box” nature limits explainability and reliability. Explainability concerns understanding the model’s decision process, including the physical meaning and contribution of extracted features, while reliability addresses the rationality and stability of diagnostic results under varying conditions. As explainability analysis reveals potential biases and irrational dependencies, it serves as the foundation for improving reliability, spurring extensive research on explainable intelligent fault diagnosis (XIFD). This survey first reviews the core components of IFD to clarify how XIFD enhances model transparency, and then categorizes existing approaches into ante-hoc and post-hoc methods. Ante-hoc methods focus on building inherently interpretable models, whereas post-hoc methods explain results through external analysis. Then, we provide the usage and disadvantages of existing post-hoc XIFD methods and emphasize the significance of ante-hoc XIFD by giving insights into the most popular signal processing-informed IFD methods. Finally, we consolidate the pressing challenges that necessitate immediate attention within the realm of XIFD research, and offer insights into promising prospects for future research endeavors. The library is available at: https://github.com/HazeDT/Awesome-Explainable-IFD-Library.

title: Predictive maintenance: A historical survey of models with imperfect inspections
abstract: The review article thoroughly examines predictive maintenance models where the conditional probabilities of inspection outcomes rely on prognostics. The demand for effective predictive maintenance models has increased due to various industries adopting data-driven strategies for improved operational effectiveness. The study retraces the historical development of these models up to significant improvements in methodologies to cover uncertainties related to inspections performed in predictive maintenance. Building on previous work, we further analyze how to input conditional probabilities of inspection outcomes into predictive maintenance modeling for better prediction of equipment breakdown and optimization of maintenance scheduling. Comparative analysis highlights a clear trade-off between model accuracy and computational complexity, showing that simpler models with the constant-probability of inspection outcomes are more interpretable but less precise, while advanced models that incorporate inspection timing, dependence on failure time, multiple time-correlated inspections, or machine learning offer higher accuracy at the expense of complexity. This synthesis also identifies the relative advantages and disadvantages of different approaches, proposing guidance for practical application in industrial systems. The article concludes by discussing future research opportunities and the potential of new technologies to enhance predictive maintenance strategies related to imperfect inspections.
keywords: Average maintenance cost per unit time

title: Evacuation under terrorist attacks: A crowd congestion control method based on deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Terrorist attacks pose severe security challenges for crowd evacuation, especially in high-density scenarios where panic-induced congestion significantly increases the number of casualties. Although existing research mainly focuses on the direct impact of attacks, the critical issue of low evacuation efficiency and increased mortality rates caused by congestion is often overlooked. Therefore, effectively regulating crowd congestion during terrorist attacks to enhance evacuation efficiency and reduce the number of casualties is a major challenge. To address this, this paper proposes a crowd congestion control method based on deep reinforcement learning under terrorist attack scenarios to enhance evacuation efficiency and safety. First, a congestion–threat coupled cellular automaton (CTCA) is constructed to simulate individual risk-avoidance behavior in a threatening environment. Second, by introducing the attack-aware Dueling Double Deep Q Network (D3QN), a congestion control method based on attack-aware D3QN and CTCA is proposed to learn optimal evacuation strategies that avoid high-risk and high-density areas. Finally, a crowd evacuation navigation system integrating CTCA and D3QN is developed. The experimental results show that the proposed method demonstrates outstanding performance in reducing congestion levels, shortening evacuation times, and lowering mortality rates. It provides theoretical support and technical tools for public safety emergency response systems.

title: A cascaded machine learning model for identification of ship breach characteristics during flooding using sensor data fusion
abstract: Water ingress in damaged ships can severely impair navigation and cause sinking. Accurate breach identification is vital for effective incident response. Due to multi-characteristic interaction of breach parameters, minor identification errors can cumulatively lead to significant inaccuracies in subsequent flooding assessment. This study proposes a cascaded machine learning model for breach identification of damaged ship using sensor data. First, the model employs temporal convolutional network to estimate floodwater volume by integrating data from internal water level and floating state sensors. Then, the model combines support vector regression and artificial neural network to identify and fine-tune breach parameters using the floodwater volume data. The hyperparameters of the models are automatically tuned based on particle swarm optimization. Strategies for training data generation and sensor fusion are explored. The model effectiveness is validated through tests on a barge under transient and progressive flooding, demonstrating consistent results with benchmark data for breach parameters and flooding consequences.

title: Dynamic ensemble model incorporating deep reinforcement learning for earthquake casualty prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of earthquake casualties is crucial to inform decision-making for efficient government rescue operations. This paper proposes a Stacking Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II Double Deep Q-Network Dynamic Ensemble (SND-DE), a unified prediction framework that integrates a two-layer Stacking architecture, Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) for multi-objective parameter optimization and a Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) decision agent for dynamic parameter selection. Within SND-DE, the ensemble prediction model utilizes a two-layer stacking structure, selecting high-performance base models and meta-models through experiments and employs a five-fold cross-validation method for prediction. A multi-objective optimization algorithm optimizes the key parameters of the prediction model, aiming to minimize both bias and variance of the prediction. Embedding the non-dominated solutions of the key parameters of the prediction model into the DDQN environment enables the model to adapt to the characteristics of different disaster scenarios and dynamically parameterize the model to reduce prediction errors. The effectiveness of the proposed model is comprehensively evaluated through a series of experiments, whose results indicate that: (1) the SND-DE model is well-trained, exhibits high predictive accuracy and achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.95279; (2) the performance of the ensemble model surpasses that of all individual base models; (3) the NSGA-II optimization algorithm effectively reduces the model's bias and variance; (4) the DDQN model exhibits strong convergence and achieves high reward values.

title: BMTR-former: Accelerating RUL prediction on scarce and censored data via bayesian-based multi-task reconstruction transformer
abstract: To overcome the limitations of data censoring in Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, we introduce BMTR-Former, a Bayesian Multi-Task Reconstruction Transformer. Our framework uniquely treats censored data not as a limitation but as a resource, integrating a supervised RUL prediction task with a self-supervised signal reconstruction task. This multi-task paradigm leverages all available trajectories to learn robust degradation patterns. The self-supervised component uses both censored and uncensored data to learn degradation patterns, enhancing RUL prediction. A hierarchical Bayesian model first denoises sensor signals to provide clean inputs for the Transformer core. Experiments show BMTR-Former excels on highly censored datasets, not only achieving state-of-the-art accuracy but also demonstrating remarkable training efficiency and rapid convergence, decisively outperforming competing models. By transforming censored data into a key asset for generalization, our work offers a new, data-efficient paradigm for industrial prognostics.

title: Data-driven transformer-based explainable deep learning model for real-time TBM performance prediction
abstract: Aiming to effectively and efficiently predict tunnel boring machine (TBM) penetration rates to assist in guiding the operation management, this research proposes TransXTBMNet, a Transformer-based explainable network designed for predicting TBM penetration rates in real-time, which integrates ensemble bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and improved Transformer to capture the complex interative relationship between operational parameters of TBM and penetration rates, enabling real-time precise predictions. Furthermore, the method encompasses various components: the data preparation process, the SHAP-based model explainability, a loss function, and performance metrics to collectively enhance robust data quality and ensure accurate predictions in dynamic excavation environments. Validation on the real TBM operation dataset demonstrates TransXTBMNet’s exceptional performance, with metrics like Mean Squared Error (MSE) = 0.2529, Root MSE (RMSE) = 0.5029, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) = 0.2991, Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) = 1.4984 %, and R2 = 0.9770. Comparative analysis shows superior results over other state-of-the-art methods such as conventional recurrent architectures (simple RNN (SRNN), GRU, LSTM) and their bidirectional variants (BiSRNN, BiGRU). SHAP analysis reveals that penetration rate at the previous time step, long with thrust groups A and F play crucial roles in predicting penetration rates. Additionally, the proposed method exhibits improved performance when considering the recorded penetration rate data, highlighting its capability to provide a better performance. Overall, the proposed method TransXTBMNet proves to be an effective and efficient solution in predicting TBM performance, providing valuable real-time guidance for optimizing TBM operations.

title: An uncertainty-guided contrastive learning method for OOD detection in trustworthy fault diagnosis
abstract: In the field of Prognostics Health Management (PHM), the “black-box” nature of deep learning-based intelligent fault diagnosis raises concerns about reliability in safety-critical applications. Traditional deterministic networks provide point estimates only, making them inadequate for quantifying prediction uncertainty and detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. To address these limitations, this paper explicitly models feature representations as Gaussian distributions, thereby preserving both predictive information and data-inherent uncertainty. Building on this foundation, we introduce a distribution-level contrastive learning strategy that enhances the separability between in-distribution and OOD samples while avoiding the challenge of negative pair selection in conventional contrastive learning. This joint design establishes a more reliable decision boundary and improves model trustworthiness. Experiments on two representative testbeds — the planetary gearbox and the main gearbox (MGB) — demonstrate that the proposed method not only achieves superior OOD detection but also maintains high in-distribution diagnostic accuracy under noisy conditions. These results highlight the method’s potential for trustworthy deployment in real-world industrial fault diagnosis.

title: A novel AI-driven framework of collaborative intelligent operation and maintenance in cloud-edge computing power networks
abstract: With the global proliferation of computing power networks driven by rapid IoT and artificial intelligence advancement, cloud-edge computing power networks (CECPN) have become critical foundations for modern digital infrastructure. However, their distributed and heterogeneous nature introduces significant cybersecurity vulnerabilities threatening data transmission reliability, thereby posing substantial challenges to operation and maintenance (O&M) management. Current research lacks comprehensive modeling across CECPN's entire data transmission lifecycle and rarely addresses heterogeneous resource allocation strategies under cyberattack scenarios. This paper proposes an AI-driven collaborative O&M framework for CECPN that optimizes multi-phase data transmission reliability recovery and costs through heterogeneous allocation of communication, computing, and operational resources under cyberattack. A case study is conducted on a 20-unit CECPN simulated environment. This study demonstrates three distinct O&M approaches: cost-oriented, reliability-oriented, and balanced strategies. The results validate the framework's capability to generate diverse solutions across various attack scenarios and recovery time windows.

title: Lightweight multimodal LLM-empowered dual-agent collaboration for reliable defect detection and maintenance recommendation in tunnel infrastructure
abstract: Accurate identification of tunnel defects and maintenance recommendations are crucial for resilient tunnel operations and sustainable urban underground development. Although numerous automated systems have been developed for tunnel defect detection, existing approaches struggle with limited semantic understanding, poor interpretability, and difficulty generating standard-compliant decisions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight multimodal LLM-empowered dual-agent collaboration framework for tunnel infrastructure maintenance, with three core innovations that advance existing research: (1) Modular Decoupling of Detection and Reasoning: We explicitly separate visual defect recognition (via a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B vision-language model) from regulatory-compliant maintenance reasoning (via a LightRAG-enhanced agent), solving the interpretability and traceability limitations of end-to-end tunnel AI systems. (2) Cost-Efficient Training & Lightweight Deployment: Using 4-bit quantization (Unsloth framework) and LoRA, we fine-tune the 7B-parameter model at ∼USD $5 per session (Google Colab Pro+) and enable real-time operation on consumer-grade GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA RTX 4050), eliminating reliance on high-end proprietary hardware. (3) LightRAG-Powered Standards-Compliant Reasoning: The LightRAG module integrates clause-level knowledge graphs and hybrid vector-graph retrieval, ensuring maintenance recommendations strictly adhere to national/regional standards (e.g., JT/T 790–2023) and mitigating LLM hallucination risks. This dual-agent design enhances tunnel resilience by enabling interpretable, scalable, and compliance-driven maintenance, with experimental validation on 8928 Shanghai tunnel images confirming superior performance over baseline models by ROUGE-1 (0.8342), ROUGE-2 (0.7389), BLEU (0.68), and semantic similarity (0.9830) scores.

title: A remaining useful life estimation method based on meta contrastive learning
abstract: Precise remaining useful life (RUL) estimation can effectively enhance the reliability and safety of industrial machinery. While deep learning methods have demonstrated strong potential in this area, their effectiveness is often limited by the scarcity of labeled data, which is both costly and time-consuming to obtain in industrial applications. Therefore, a novel RUL estimation method based on meta contrastive learning is proposed to construct an efficient semi-supervised learning process, which specifically targets the challenges of limited labeled data by deeply mining the underlying degradation information within the vast amounts of unlabeled data. First, a meta contrastive learning algorithm is proposed to ensure that the contrastive information derived from unlabeled data positively influence the model’s performance on labeled data. Meanwhile, a meta-update strategy is designed to mitigate overfitting and catastrophic forgetting, effectively improving the feature extraction potential and generalization ability of deep learning structures. Additionally, a weight optimization strategy is proposed to adaptively adjust the weight factor of the semi-supervised learning process based on the performance of the supervised task, thus enhancing the flexibility and effectiveness of semi-supervised learning. The proposed method is validated on the turbofan engine and wind turbine gearbox datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and superiority.

title: Risk source identification and prevention for metro driven by large language models: A new approach to enhancing system reliability and safety
abstract: Hazard source identification in metro operation and maintenance faces challenges like high data dimensionality, data heterogeneity and difficult data structuring. Existing general knowledge graphs fail to fully consider domain - specific business logic, leading to low identification accuracy and frequent catastrophic incidents. To solve this, this paper develops a new identification method based on the dual knowledge self -verification large language model, which boosts accuracy and enables efficient targeted control. It establishes a three - dimensional “root cause – hazard source - hazardous event” framework, integrates In - Context Learning with Chain of Thought for reasoning, uses Transformer multi - head self - attention to extract knowledge triplets, applies dual verification to build hierarchical causal knowledge graphs, and creates a risk quantification model. Validation with metro data shows domain knowledge extraction has an 86.6% F1 score (18.1% higher than UIE model). Targeting the critical “inadequate management and maintenance” node (78.4% of cumulative disaster severity weight) cuts accident rate by 16.66%. This research enables a shift from passive to proactive metro disaster risk control.

title: A sample-efficient transfer learning framework for industrial remaining useful life prediction leveraging large language models
abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is fundamental to industrial Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). However, existing models struggle to process high-dimensional, multi-condition sensor data, generalize across varying operating conditions, and perform well with limited labeled data. To address these challenges, we propose a sample-efficient RUL prediction framework based on a transferable Large Language Model (LLM), which captures complex temporal dependencies in sensor data while reducing pre-processing requirements. The framework integrates two core innovations: a transferable LLM backbone that automates feature extraction from complex sensor data, and a dual-score sample selection strategy that significantly improves learning efficiency by identifying the most informative samples for transfer learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the framework achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance across diverse operating conditions using a single hyperparameter configuration, significantly reducing the computational overhead and domain expertise requirements that limit the scalability of existing methods. Beyond predictive accuracy, this study offers insights into its internal mechanisms, showing how it dynamically prioritizes sensor data to capture critical degradation patterns across varying conditions. These findings enhance model interpretability by linking data-driven predictions to physical processes. By addressing key challenges such as data efficiency, feature extraction, and transferability, the framework offers a reliable solution for industrial signal processing, improving the cost-effectiveness and robustness of PHM strategies across diverse operational domains.

title: An aero-engine remaining useful life prediction method based on deformable convolutional residual attention enhanced Kolmogorov-Arnold networks with prediction advance and shape constraints
abstract: Improving the practicality and reliability of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction requires achieving more accurate, earlier, and more relevant forecasts. However, existing methods are limited by the weak feature extraction ability of fully connected layers and the inability of conventional loss functions to balance early prediction and trend consistency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a prediction model base on deformable convolutional residual attention (DCRA) modules with Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KAN). An early prediction and shape constraint loss function (ESLF) is further designed to enhance model reliability. Specifically, the DCRA module adaptively extracts multi-scale degradation features through deformable convolution kernels, while KAN serves as a regressor to improve feature mapping. Moreover, the main spline function of KAN reflects the occurrence of degradation, thereby improving model interpretability. The proposed ESLF is asymmetric and improves the similarity between predicted and actual RUL sequences. Comparative and ablation experiments conducted on the CMAPSS and NCMAPSS datasets verify the superior prediction performance of the proposed method. The average RMSE and Score are reduced by 5.19 % and 9.28 % on CMAPSS, and by 4.63 % and 9.47 % on NCMAPSS, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed approach in practical health management scenarios.

title: Self-data-driven remaining useful life prediction of rotating machinery under time-varying operating conditions based on a two-stage hybrid state-space model
abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is the foundation of predictive maintenance and provides an effective way to reduce operational and maintenance costs. However, time-varying operating conditions (TVOCs) and limited run-to-failure data at industrial sites significantly hinder the performance of traditional RUL prediction methods. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel self-data-driven RUL prediction method for rotating machinery (RM) under TVOCs. First, inspired by time-varying response systems in control theory, a two-stage hybrid state-space model (HSSM) is developed by combining the dynamic modeling capabilities of state-space models with the nonlinear fitting ability of neural networks. This model innovatively integrates TVOCs into the mathematical formulation of the dynamic degradation process of RM. It aims to describe the functional relationship among operating conditions, system states, and response signals during the entire life cycle of RM under TVOCs, thereby avoiding the impact on RUL prediction caused by the coupling of operating conditions and system states. Then, based on the extended Kalman filter algorithm and the monitoring data generated by the system itself, an alternating parameter update strategy is introduced to solve the system state within the HSSM, enabling real-time tracking of RM degradation. Furthermore, an adaptive model selection strategy is proposed to dynamically identify the optimal state degradation model. This method effectively overcomes the problem of insufficient historical run-to-failure data for offline model training. In addition, the design characteristics of the HSSM at different stages provide an integrated solution for both anomaly detection and RUL prediction in RM. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are validated through both simulation and experimental studies.

title: A prediction strategy for embankment piping occurrence based on comprehensive feature selection and machine learning
abstract: Piping is a critical hazard in embankment structures, posing risks to public safety. Traditional piping prediction models are often computationally complex and time-consuming. This study proposed a piping occurrence prediction strategy that integrates feature selection and machine learning (ML) to monitor embankment conditions. Taking the Yangtze River embankment as the dataset, comprehensive feature selection techniques (including Pearson analysis, random forest feature importance, and SHAP values) were employed to analyze the importance and correlation of factors influencing piping. The influential factors were ranked as follows: overburden thickness H (0.32), void ratio e (0.24), water level difference ∆h (0.17), compressibility coefficient av (0.12), dry density ρd (0.07), and effective cohesion c'(0.03). To address the impact of an imbalance dataset on the ML prediction model, variational autoencoder (VAE) technology was used to process the original piping data, ensuring a balance dataset. To develop an accurate prediction model, the parameters of backpropagation (BP), support vector machines (SVM), and EXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were optimized using genetic algorithms (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and grey wolf optimization (GWO). The research results showed that the GA-XGBoost model achieved the best performance, with an R2 of 0.96, RMSE of 0.10, and MAE of 0.06 on the Yangxin validation set. And the proposed model outperformed existing methods on prediction accuracy. Additionally, a piping prediction platform was developed, providing an intuitive interface that facilitates quick retrieval of predictions, enabling engineers to make informed decisions with ease.

title: AK-TSYS: An enhanced active learning Kriging model for time-dependent system reliability analysis
abstract: Complex engineering systems involve multiple failure modes, components, and temporal parameters, all of which pose significant challenges for time-dependent system reliability analysis (TDSRA). In this study, a novel framework named AK-TSYS, an active learning Kriging-based method for TDSRA, is proposed to enhance the conventional AK-MCS (active learning combining Kriging and Monte Carlo simulation) framework. Within the proposed method, initial training samples are selected to construct Kriging models for all failure modes. A two-stage active learning strategy is then adopted: in the global exploration stage, a hybrid learning function integrates composite expected least global (ELG) and expected improvement (EI) functions to identify optimal random variables, time instances, and failure mode indexes; the subsequent local exploitation defines a localized region around the candidate global optimal point to find a higher-quality learning point, thereby iteratively refining the surrogate model. The training process terminates when an error-based system stopping criterion is satisfied, ensuring convergence with improved computational efficiency and accuracy. The system failure probability is finally estimated using the system structure functions, which are applicable to series, parallel, and mixed systems. The AK-TSYS is demonstrated through three numerical examples and four practical applications, including a parallel Daniels system, a remote vector reducer, mixed systems, and a series system analyzed by finite element simulation. Furthermore, a sensitivity analysis systematically evaluates the influence of key parameters, including the stopping criterion threshold, initial training points, and local exploitation radius. Based on the findings, practical implementation guidelines of AK-TSYS are provided.

title: A self-calibrating digital twin for space thermionic nuclear reactors under fault conditions
abstract: Space nuclear power systems operate unattended for extended periods, making them susceptible to failures. Furthermore, spatial constraints necessitate sparse sensor deployment, which makes comprehensive operational status monitoring difficult. Therefore, a Digital Twin (DT) model capable of characterizing the system's unmeasurable states is crucial for ensuring its reliability and operational safety. Faults or performance degradation can introduce parameter uncertainties that severely compromise DT accuracy. To address this, a DT model for a space thermionic nuclear reactor (STNR) has been developed. This model is underpinned by a physics-based mechanism model and incorporates Transformer and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to achieve initial state synchronization. Furthermore, an online calibration mechanism is implemented using Model Predictive Control (MPC) and the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES). Following sensitivity analysis to identify adjustable parameters, CMA-ES then finds the optimal parameters that minimize deviation, thereby correcting the transient evolution behavior of the STNR. The root mean squared error (RMSE) for state synchronization on the test set was under 0.0878, and the relative errors of online calibration under fault conditions were below 0.6 %. Furthermore, noise tests and fault sensitivity analyses were conducted, confirming the method meets engineering requirements. Therefore, the method shows promising potential in deep space exploration.

title: Innovative defense strategies: Fusion deep learning approach to counter false data injection attacks in power systems
abstract: A pervasive threat to power systems is the occurrence of False Data Injection Attacks (FDIA), which can disrupt the underlying control infrastructure and endanger the reliability of the system. Many efforts have been made to combat FDIAs. However, most of the reported methods have some shortcomings that prevent them from being used in real-world applications, such as scalability issues, resource constraints, and privacy concerns, which hinder their practical applicability. In this paper, a novel Fusion Deep Learning (FDL) method is applied to the detection of FDIAs, enabling real-time deployment with high accuracy, low memory overhead, and fast model convergence. The proposed framework employs a confidence-aware, memory-based fusion strategy that enhances robustness to non-IID data, concept drift, and realistic disturbances. It demonstrates strong generalization by accurately distinguishing cyber-attacks from natural variations such as sensor noise and topological changes, thereby reducing false positives. More importantly, no data is transmitted to the control center during optimization of the FDIA detection model to maintain data privacy. The performance of the proposed method is compared with the Centralized Deep Learning model based on Convolutional Neural Network as a representative of centralized approaches. The evaluation of the proposed method was performed on the IEEE 118-bus power network, a real dataset of the New York Independent System Operator. Through numerical evaluation, our findings not only affirm the superiority of FDL in accuracy, data storage efficiency, and convergence speed but also underscore its potential to revolutionize security strategies in modern power infrastructures.

title: A generative modeling method to quantify the long-term benefit of neural-network-based RUL predictions to maintenance
abstract: Many remaining useful life (RUL) prediction models rely on neural networks. These models focus on predictive accuracy at the component level, but their impact on system-level maintenance remains underexplored. Quantifying this effect is difficult because maintenance decisions are often optimized from long-term simulations. These simulations do not provide real-time measurements for RUL prediction, making direct use of specific prognostic models challenging. To address this gap, we propose a maintenance optimization framework that uses generative modeling with a generative adversarial network (GAN) to create realistic prognostic trajectories for system-level cost assessment. Feature adaptation is added to the GAN to ensure that generated trajectories retain key statistical properties, such as accuracy, timeliness, and credibility, seen in actual model evaluations. This framework allows the benefits of prognostic models to be assessed probabilistically and offers guidance on whether to include prognostics in maintenance planning. A case study on wind farm maintenance demonstrates the effectiveness of the method. Although the wind farm example considers only limited subsystem dependencies, the framework is not restricted to this configuration. The approach is flexible and can be extended to systems with more complex dependencies by adjusting maintenance policies.

title: EnergyMatch: A long-tailed semi-supervised learning framework for cross-domain fault diagnosis
abstract: Achieving nearly-unbiased fault diagnosis with long-tailed labeled source domain is vital. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) methods, leveraging pseudo-labeling and consistency regularization, offer promising solutions for handling imbalanced data. However, variations in working conditions cause feature distribution shifts and potential class distribution shifts in the unlabeled target domain, where the specific class distribution remains unknown. These challenges significantly diminish the performance of conventional SSL methods. To address these issues, we propose EnergyMatch, a novel long-tailed SSL framework for cross-domain fault diagnosis under unknown target class distributions. EnergyMatch builds upon a classic SSL method FixMatch, which uses pseudo labels of weakly augmented instances to train strongly augmented ones. We introduce a double-classifier architecture: the balanced classifier dynamically estimates the target class distribution to guide logit adjustment for pseudo labels generated by the standard classifier. Additionally, we design two energy-based strategies: a free energy-based alignment loss to mitigate feature distribution shifts and an energy-based instance removal module to discard high-uncertainty instances and select more reliable pseudo-labeled instances with dynamically adjusted confidence thresholds. Extensive experiments on bearing and gearbox datasets validate the proposed EnergyMatch, demonstrating its effectiveness in addressing distribution shifts and improving classification performance in challenging scenarios under varying target class distributions.

title: Development of surrogate models in probabilistic risk assessment accounting explicitly for the effect of surveillance test intervals
abstract: Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA) is an efficient tool for assessing, maintaining, and improving the safety of Nuclear Power Plants (NPPs). PRA applications have been identified in the literature, such as supporting NPP testing and maintenance planning and optimization, in-service testing, risk monitoring, etc. These applications typically involve extending the level of detail for analyzing specific issues, such as aging trends, updating reliability models and parameters, and adjusting test strategies, imperfect maintenance policies, etc., which is an unaffordable challenge for most commercial PRA codes because of their lack of flexibility in modeling such complex scenarios. In addition, such applications often require quantifying the underlying models and data many times, and this is done with a high computational cost. Surrogate models or metamodeling techniques emerge as an alternative approach to address this limitation. The objective of this study is to develop a surrogate model using supervised machine learning algorithms to estimate the Core Damage Frequency (CDF), emulating the commercial code-based level 1 PRA model calculation function. Three machine learning models, Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine are evaluated using data concerning level 1 PRA basic parameters such as component failure rates and probabilities of failure on demand, human error probabilities, and standby equipment test intervals. The findings highlight the flexibility and effectiveness of some of these models in estimating CDF considering explicitly the effect of surveillance test intervals.

title: Change point severity-aware remaining useful life prediction
abstract: • A severity-aware framework for change point-based RUL estimation is proposed. • Normalized Euclidean Distance is used to quantify severity of the changepoint. • Severity levels guide model specialization in LSTM-based RUL prediction. As a cornerstone of the upcoming industrial revaluation, predictive maintenance leverages intelligent systems and real-time data processing to transform traditional industrial operations. A fundamental part of this maintenance strategy is estimating the Remaining Useful Life (RUL), which is the time remaining before a component or system requires maintenance or replacement. The onset of the degradation process, termed the change point, serves as a significant preliminary step for reliable RUL estimation of complex machinery. Existing works are often limited to only detecting the change point, without considering the intensity or severity of the change that occurs. In this work, we propose a novel framework that integrates severity-aware change detection into the RUL estimation process. The Normalized Euclidean Distance (NED) metric is introduced to quantify the severity of each change point, enabling a more accurate estimation of system degradation. This information is incorporated into a long short-term memory (LSTM)- based RUL estimation approach, allowing predictions to adapt based on the intensity of degradation in change points. Experimental evaluations on C-MAPSS benchmark datasets show that our method enhances prediction accuracy against state-of-the-art LSTM methods.

title: An unsupervised long-tailed fine-grained few-shot fault diagnosis method based on feature space adjustment strategy
abstract: In the operation of mechanical equipment, fault data often display an implicit long-tailed distribution, making manual labeling labor-intensive. Moreover, traditional fault diagnosis methods struggle to identify fault causes from a fine-grained perspective without labels. Based on those, an unsupervised long-tailed fine-grained few-shot fault diagnosis method, USL-F4SA, is proposed, which dynamically enhances batches through a queue mechanism and applies indicators and auxiliary sets to construct a class balance mechanism in the feature space. Initially, K-means clustering identifies cluster centers of the original training set, the sparsity of clustering features is used to detect tail classes. Samples with high cosine similarity to the original training set are selected from an auxiliary dataset to balance the distribution of tail classes. Then, a dynamic queue is introduced to find the nearest neighbor for each sample, which is added as a positive sample to the batch. The optimal transport algorithm samples the queue, ensuring optimal assignment between current batch embeddings and the queue, allowing dynamic adaptation to new data. Finally, an indicator assigns indexes to all samples, ensuring correct sample pairing and distinguishing samples from different distributions. Validated on public datasets, USL-F4SA outperforms state-of-the-art methods in predicting unseen fine-grained faults (code available at https://github.com/zhiqan/USL-F4SA).

title: Improved AHP and dual-hidden layer adaptive regularized neural network model for the quantitative risk assessment of oil and gas pipelines
abstract: Conventional risk assessment of oil and gas pipelines primarily relies on expert judgment, which suffers from limited generalizability, high uncertainty and subjectivity, frequently leading to imprecise outcomes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a risk evaluation model (ImAHP-DHARN) for oil and gas pipelines based on an improved analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and a dual-hidden-layer adaptive regularized neural network (DHARN) model. First, a dynamic frequency-consequence matrix is employed to enable dynamic updates of risk values using five significant key factors: corrosion factor, structural defect, third party damage, natural disaster, and physical damage. Second, AHP is integrated with a comprehensive weighting framework to determine indicator weights, offering improved accuracy. Third, the DHARN model is developed, incorporating tansig-Softmax activation, L2 regularization, and early stopping to mitigate overfitting. Finally, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) module is implemented to interpret model outputs and quantify the relative importance of indicators, providing insights into risk prioritization. The proposed ImAHP-DHARN model was validated using PHMSA pipeline accident data, achieving an accuracy of 98.3 %, outperforming SVM (93.3 %) and LVQ (98.0 %). In Monte Carlo adversarial testing (e.g., earthquake scenarios superimposed with internal corrosion), the model exhibits a misjudgment rate of only 1.3 %, underscoring its robustness. The SHAP analysis further highlights corrosion prevention T3 as the highest-priority risk factor, providing valuable reference for pipeline risk management. In summary, the ImAHP-DHARN model significantly enhances the objectivity, generalization capability, robustness of pipeline risk assessment. Beyond this domain, this methodology can be extended to other complex industrial systems, providing a robust framework for risk assessment.

title: Application of interactive threat matrix induced system dynamics model to determine risk probability and resilient policy measures for CO2 pipelines
abstract: In the sphere of decarbonization, a comprehensive CO 2 (Carbon dioxide) pipeline risk analysis framework is crucial for resilient long-term operations. Canadian Standards Association (CSA) updated regulations Z662:23 requires operators and regulatory bodies to develop quantitative risk assessment methodologies with probability and consequence analysis. Thus, this study is aimed at determining risk probability of CO 2 pipelines across Canada, while developing a simulation tool for consecutive policy analysis. The process involves integration of threat matrix from real gas pipeline incident dataset, long-short term memory (LSTM) model and system dynamics (SD) simulation. Baseline simulation represents a risk probability value of 5.89 with a synthetic integrity of 55.1 % by 2055. Sensitivity analysis, calibration, scenario analysis and structural validity have been performed to check the numerical boundary adequacy, accuracy and variability of the built SD model. Among two policies simulated, Policy 2 has been found to be more resilient, as it restrained the risk probability to a value of 2.54 with an increased 77.4 % pipeline integrity. The developed methodology is a simplified risk probability analysis tool for CO₂ pipelines, with extensible features to incorporate further consequences and economic analysis.

title: Prediction of navigation aid malfunction based on hash chain-optimized FP-growth and gradient boosting random forest
abstract: Causal analysis and prediction of navigation aid malfunctions are essential for waterway safety and maritime traffic efficiency. Existing research has largely been confined to shallow analyses of navigation aid status perception and factors influencing malfunctions, lacking in-depth exploration of the complex nonlinear causal mechanism, which limits the capability for high-precision prediction of navigation aid malfunctions. To address this issue, this study first developed a hash chain-optimized directional constraint FP-growth algorithm to mine association rules between the causes and the malfunctions. Then, the extracted rules were integrated as features into the original dataset for data augmentation. Finally, this study employed a hyperparameter-optimized gradient boosting random forest algorithm to predict navigation aid malfunctions. The results indicate that ship collision is the primary cause of navigation aid malfunctions, and river discharge is the key environmental factor. Moreover, through improvements in data augmentation and algorithm optimization, the proposed method outperforms the baseline model, achieving improvements of 8.6 %, 7.4 %, 6.3 %, 8.2 %, 4.7 %, and 7.6 % in Precision, Recall, F1-Score, Accuracy, AUC, and AUPR, respectively. This research methodology effectively identifies the key causes of navigation aid malfunctions and enhances prediction accuracy, providing robust decision support for the intelligent maintenance of navigation aids and waterway safety management.

title: Causal modeling and risk assessment of runway excursion events via interpretable machine learning
abstract: Runway excursions remain a persistent threat to flight safety and operational reliability. The causal chains behind these events are often unclear under complex weather and workload conditions. This study identifies and quantifies the triggers and pathways that lead to runway excursion risk. We analyze 1345 Boeing 737-700 flights using Quick Access Recorder data. An XGBoost model with SHAP values screens nonlinear drivers. We then apply the Independent Component Analysis Linear Non-Gaussian Acyclic model to infer directed and weighted links among sequential exceedances. A Bayesian network estimates trigger probabilities, average treatment effects, and joint risks. Our main contribution is the integration of interpretable learning and causal discovery in a single, queryable graph. Results confirm key triggers: angle of attack asymmetry, elevated radio altitude near touchdown, and delayed thrust reverser deployment. The network shows path dependence, convergence from multiple sources, and escalation along high-impact chains. In a counterfactual policy test, we increase the share of landings with normal bank and a normal 50 ft to touchdown distance by 1.5 percent and reduce the share with small bank and long float by 1 percent. This lowers the estimated probability of severe excessive total landing distance from 11.7 percent to 10.0 percent. A 1 percent increase in the favorable scenario lowers this probability by 0.14 percentage points. Findings remain stable in robust bootstrap tests and noise sensitivity checks. These insights support targeted training and procedures that prioritize touchdown precision and timely deceleration. The framework provides quantitative and reproducible guidance for reliability-centered runway safety management.

title: Fragility analysis of dam-reservoir systems under seismic loading using LSTM-integrated model order reduction
abstract: Seismic analysis of dam-reservoir systems considering fluid-structure interactions and nonlinear material behavior is crucial for safety assessment. It requires a three-dimensional full-scale model capable of capturing various failure modes, considering various uncertainties. Fragility analysis, routinely used in a probabilistic framework, is computationally very expensive because of the size and need for repeated simulations. This issue is addressed here using a combination of reduced order modeling (ROM), machine learning, and high-performance computing using CPU and GPU. Accordingly, a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) based non-intrusive ROM is integrated with LSTM for high dimensional regression. Two new modifications to an existing framework are proposed here. First, force-feeding system parameter information in the LSTM, and second, adopting two-step singular value decomposition for large systems. A model of the Koyna dam of varying complexities — from 2D linear to 3D nonlinear models with more than 105 degrees of freedom — under non-stationary excitations is considered for numerical studies. The nonlinearity is modeled using a continuum plasticity-based damage model. The proposed methodology is scalable, and achieves a computational speed-up of three orders of magnitude compared to the full-scale analysis. The non-intrusive nature of the method allows usage of any black box or commercial code.

title: When agents learn to think: Large language model-enhanced agent-based modeling for crowd evacuation in disaster scenarios
abstract: Reliable and realistic modeling of crowd evacuation is critical for improving the safety and resilience of complex transportation and infrastructure systems under disaster emergencies. Traditional agent-based modeling has been widely used to simulate individual behaviors and interactions during evacuations, but often struggles to represent interpersonal communication, context-aware reasoning, and adaptive decision-making under rapidly evolving conditions. To address these limitations, this study introduces a dynamic evacuation simulation framework that integrates large language models as decision-making cores for individual agents. Each agent maintains personality traits, environmental observations, and decision histories, while the large language model enables context-sensitive reasoning and information exchange between agents and their surroundings. To support large-scale, computationally efficient simulations, we implement batch prompting and parallel processing strategies that reduce runtime overhead. Both pedestrian and vehicle evacuations are represented to capture multimodal evacuation dynamics. Using a real-world disaster evacuation case study, we demonstrate that incorporating large language models significantly enhances the realism, adaptability, and reliability of evacuation simulations. The framework reduces reliance on manually defined behavioral rules, supports probabilistic safety and reliability assessment, and provides a scalable platform for stress-testing evacuation strategies under diverse hazard scenarios. This research bridges the gap between human-centered behavioral modeling and engineering decision-support, offering a novel tool for disaster preparedness and resilience planning.

title: A Machine learning-based framework for reliability prediction of metallic seals with manufacturing-induced dimensional uncertainties
abstract: Metal seals, as core components in precision and safety-critical systems, have inherent variability in geometric dimensions due to processing tolerances and manufacturing limitations, which in turn leads to significant uncertainties in structural performance. Facing this challenge, traditional reliability assessment methods have deficiencies in high-dimensional uncertainty characterization, nonlinear coupling effect capture, and the balance between computational efficiency and accuracy. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel machine learning-based reliability evaluation framework specifically tailored to metal seals affected by manufacturing-induced variations. The proposed methodology integrates (1) advanced Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) and high-fidelity finite element modeling to systematically quantify the impact of geometric uncertainties on structural performance, and (2) a comprehensive comparison between conventional machine learning algorithms and automated machine learning (AutoML) approaches, with an emphasis on hyperparameter optimization and generalization capability. Results indicate that the Auto-Sklearn-based AutoML model delivers superior performance across diverse material properties and tolerance configurations, achieving high-accuracy prediction of reliability curves (mean squared error < 0.0042) and precise estimation of minimum tensile strength required to ensure 99 % reliability (relative error < 3.25 %). Furthermore, computational analysis reveals that employing 200 U-profile coordinate points and 2000 training samples provides an optimal trade-off between model accuracy and efficiency. This study establishes a data-driven, scalable paradigm for reliability prediction under stochastic manufacturing conditions, and offers practical guidelines for material selection and structural design of metallic seals in precision engineering applications.

title: A novel multiaxial fatigue life prediction method based on multi-scale physical neural network
abstract: A new multi-scale physical neural network is proposed to address the structural limitations of current physical neural networks in the task of multiaxial fatigue life prediction. These limitations primarily arise from the singular scale of the fusion approach between physical information and neural networks, coupled with its inflexible structural design, which results in restricted generalization capability and stability. This multi-scale physical neural network mainly consists of the multi-scale embedded physical neural network and the association-capturing neural network. The multi-scale embedded one is used to obtain physical parameters and high-fidelity parameters, while the other one is used to capture the causal dependencies between these parameters and enhance the model mapping capabilities. In addition, a novel physical loss function is proposed to direct the iterative optimization process and bolster the model’s predictive stability. Fifteen datasets are utilized to validate the model’s prediction performance. The proposed model demonstrates superior generalization capability and stability in performance comparisons with eight other models.

title: Data-driven copula Bayesian network for risk analysis of lithium-ion battery accidents
abstract:
Abstract:
Owing to their high energy density, low self-discharge rate and long service life, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are extensively employed. With the surge of application scope, the safety issues of LIBs have received increasing attention, especially thermal runaway accidents. Risk analysis on thermal runaway accidents is beneficial to develop the risk control measures of batteries. With the availability of accident statistics, data-driven approach can reduce the reliance on expert experience. The copula function can capture nonlinear features to characterize model uncertainty. This article proposes a data-driven copula Bayesian network (DCBN) model for risk analysis of LIB accidents. First, we collect records of battery thermal runaway accidents and process the data containing multiple failure modes and risk-influencing factors (RIFs). Second, we use copula functions to model the correlations between variables, particularly the nonlinear relationships between variables. Subsequently, we introduce the data-driven method to depict causal relationships between RIFs. Eventually, we establish a Bayesian network (BN) model with correlation analysis, predictive analysis, and diagnostic analysis to evaluate the probability distribution of fault modes and their impact on risk status. We conduct a case study using LIB data from the aviation domain. The results show that this model can assess risk on LIB accidents and support for battery risk control.

title: AI-enhanced RUL prediction of PEMFCs under dynamic operating conditions using XGBoost-based HI extraction and hybrid transformer-GRU model
abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) are critical for zero-emission energy systems, particularly in electro-hydrogen generators (GEH2). Accurate Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is crucial for ensuring operational reliability and enabling predictive maintenance. However, dynamic operating conditions present a significant challenge for existing prognostic approaches, particularly in extracting robust Health Indicators (HIs). Conventional HIs, often based on voltage or power, are highly sensitive to mission profiles and fail to generalize in real-world conditions. To address this limitation, we propose a novel data-driven approach based on XGBoost regression to extract a degradation-specific HI directly from raw voltage measurements. This method effectively filters out transient fluctuations caused by varying power demands, isolating the true degradation trend without requiring complex preprocessing or domain expertise. Leveraging the extracted HI, we introduce a hybrid deep learning model that combines Transformer networks and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) to capture temporal dependencies and provide accurate RUL predictions under dynamic conditions. Explainable AI techniques are integrated to interpret the model’s predictions and analyze the influence of operational variables on fuel cell degradation. The proposed framework is validated on a real-world industrial dataset from four PEMFC stacks operating in GEH2 systems. Experimental results demonstrate superior accuracy, robustness, and generalizability compared to state-of-the-art methods, highlighting the potential of this scalable and interpretable approach for predictive maintenance in complex industrial environments.

title: A GNN-boosted reinforcement learning framework for maintenance optimization in multi-dependency manufacturing system
abstract: Maintenance optimization in manufacturing systems faces challenges due to multiple dependencies, including cost-sharing in maintenance operations, interactive degradation across interconnected machines, and competition for limited spare part resources. These interdependencies, together with high-dimensional decision spaces and evolving system dynamics, limit the effectiveness of conventional optimization methods such as heuristic scheduling rules and Markov decision processes (MDPs). Existing studies rarely address these heterogeneous dependencies in a unified framework. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a Multi-Hierarchical Graph Neural Network–based reinforcement learning framework (MHGNN-PPO) for dependency-aware maintenance decision optimization. Specifically, MHGNN constructs a multi-layered graph to explicitly represent economic, stochastic, and resource dependencies. By combining hierarchical graph structures with cross-graph attention aggregation, MHGNN dynamically captures intricate inter-machine relationships and refines system state representations. Furthermore, a constraint-integrated and stability-enhanced PPO algorithm is developed to ensure feasible decision-making and reliable convergence in high-dimensional maintenance environments. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, an experiment was conducted on a manufacturing system consisting of 24 machines. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed MHGNN-PPO framework achieves higher cumulative rewards than baseline methods, while maintaining convergence stability across different system scales. Ablation studies revealed that excluding any component notably gains lower rewards, highlighting the necessity of explicit dependency modeling. Additionally, robustness tests further validate the adaptability and resilience of MHGNN-PPO under varying dependency intensities.

title: Adaptive turbofan engine health assessment for multi-component performance degradation coupling scenarios: A spatiotemporal attention graph convolutional network approach
abstract: Aircraft turbofan engines are essential components that directly influence flight safety through their operational health. The complex functional and structural coupling among internal components results in interconnected performance degradation, manifesting as distinct spatial patterns in sensor monitoring data. Operating under extreme conditions of high temperature, high pressure, and sustained high-speed rotation, these engines experience temporal variations in thermodynamic states and mechanical properties, creating temporal dependencies in the monitoring data. Traditional health assessment methods face significant challenges in processing comprehensive performance state information, as data perturbations can compromise both evaluation accuracy and stability, resulting in health trends that fail to reflect the engine's actual degradation state. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces a Spatiotemporal Attention Graph Convolutional Network (STAGCN) method, which combines spatiotemporal attention mechanisms with graph convolutions. This integration enables adaptive feature reduction and precise quantification of turbofan engine health states under complex, time-varying conditions and multi-component degradation coupling scenarios. The STAGCN utilizes attention mechanism's correlation-mining and focus capabilities to identify high-relevance regions of performance degradation within high-dimensional, long-sequence monitoring data, thereby enhancing assessment accuracy through adaptive extraction of dense degradation information.
