Second, an interpretable cross-domain transfer learning model is constructed by embedding a self-attention mechanism and a Bayesian linear layer into the domain adaptation framework, which enhances robustness in cross-domain prediction and mitigates overfitting under few-shot conditions in the target domain. Finally, a lightweight analysis method for identifying critical time steps and feature contributions is established to further improve the interpretability of the decision-making process. Experimental results on the IEEE PHM 2012 bearing dataset and the XJTU-SY bearing dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving an RMSE of 0.06, an MAE of 0.05, and an R² of 0.96.

title: Optimizing post-disaster road restoration with reinforcement learning: A traveler-behavior-aware approach
abstract: This paper introduces an AI-driven method to optimize short-term road network restoration in disaster-affected areas, aiming to maximize post-disaster traffic acceleration. Our approach considers travelers' behavior, gradual adaptation to network changes, limited recovery resources, and uncertainties in recovery times. Addressing these complexities requires a stochastic approach for uncertainties, sequential decision-making for resource management, and a model-free technique for simulating traveler adaptation. To tackle these challenges, we develop the Traveler-Adaptive Restoration Mechanism (TARM), integrating Reinforcement Learning (RL), the Markov Decision Process (MDP), and optimization-based day-to-day traffic simulation. The method is evaluated on Sioux Falls' road network under tornado scenarios based on historical data. Results highlight the influence of travelers’ route choices and the speed of restoration information dissemination on optimal policies. Findings reveal that accelerating the road restoration process by increasing restoration resources does not necessarily enhance the traffic movement efficiency in disaster-affected communities during the disaster response period. Furthermore, we demonstrate that contrary to exiting studies, shortening restoration period is not an appropriate measure of efficiency for post-disaster restoration operations. In fact, reducing the restoration period may adversely impact traffic movements during the response phase in post-disaster situations.

title: Data-driven robust design optimization of 3D frequency selective surfaces under hybrid uncertainties
abstract: Conventional design approaches for frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) often neglect the influence of uncertainties on electromagnetic (EM) response, particularly those arising from material property variations, manufacturing-induced geometric deviations, and changes in wave incidence angles. Without accounting for these inherent uncertainties, FSSs risk sub-optimal performance or even failure to filter EM waves across the intended frequency range. To address this challenge, we propose a robust design framework that optimizes the worst-case performance of FSSs under combined material, geometric, and incidence-angle uncertainties. Specifically, the first two statistical moments of normalized bandwidth and average transmittance are optimized simultaneously in the worst-case scenario. To mitigate the prohibitive computational cost of full-wave simulations for 3D FSSs, a data-driven surrogate modelling approach, extreme-aware Kriging (XK), is developed. XK adaptively selects new sampling points during training to achieve high prediction accuracy across the entire design space, including at extreme boundaries. Leveraging this robust framework, the optimized FSSs exhibit ultrawide, dual-polarized passbands with high transmittance while maintaining strong robustness to uncertainties. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed robust design optimization approach in realising more reliable FSS structures.

title: System reliability analysis with active learning: A one-step look-ahead policy based on expected uncertainty reduction function
abstract: System reliability analysis aims to evaluate the failure probability of engineering systems with uncertain inputs and multiple failure modes. Kriging-based active learning methods have shown high efficiency for component-level reliability but face challenges at the system level due to interactions among limit state functions. In this work, in line with the principle of the one-step look-ahead policy, a novel Kriging-based active learning method is proposed for system reliability analysis. Two key measures are derived: an upper bound of the sample misclassification probability, which quantifies the probability of incorrectly classifying the signs of sample responses, and its integral over the input space, which quantifies the uncertainty in the estimated failure probability. Building on these metrics, an Expected Uncertainty Reduction (EUR) function is developed to evaluate the potential contribution of each candidate sample-component pair in improving the accuracy of failure probability estimation. Additionally, a global convergence criterion is proposed to ensure the accuracy of the estimated failure probability before stopping the learning process. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through several numerical and engineering examples. The results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy while requiring fewer performance function evaluations compared with existing approaches.

title: Risk-informed opportunistic operation and maintenance for floating offshore wind turbine towers subjected to corrosion fatigue
abstract: Floating Offshore Wind Turbines (FOWTs) promise abundant wind resources in deep waters but face structural risks due to corrosion-fatigue (CF) deterioration. The present study aims at a comprehensive framework to evaluate and mitigate the CF risk, and to optimise the operational costs and power production through incorporating strategic and window-aligned the opportunistic operation and maintenance (OOM). Multi-physics modelling and reliability assessment are applied to evaluate fracture-critical ring-flange connections at component, flange, and structural levels. On this basis, failure risk is further quantified through cost losses associated with varying failure consequences. As the key factor influencing structural vibration and power production, three turbine control strategies are examined, i.e., a reference strategy and two de-rating strategies with varying operational reductions. Based on these risk-informed insights, a Genetic Algorithm (GA)-driven, co-scheduled OOM framework is proposed to optimise both turbine control strategies and maintenance actions in an integrated manner. The results highlight the critical impact of CF deterioration on the structural reliability and risk over a 25-year service life. Meanwhile, the de-rating control strategy is validated in mitigating the structural risk and extending maintenance intervals. By coupling operation strategies with maintenance actions in a risk-informed and window-aligned way, a delicate trade-off can be achieved to optimise the structural risk, maintenance cost, and power production in a life-cycle context. This study provides practical insights for industry, demonstrating risk-informed OOM strategies can enhance FOWT performance and cost-effectiveness under similar design and environmental conditions. The proposed framework also sets the stage for future research on dynamic maintenance strategies in FOWT risk and reliability management.

title: Revealing the dynamics and multidimensional resilience of rainstorm-flood cascade disasters in mountain valley cities: An interpretable machine learning case study from Southwestern China
abstract: Extreme rainstorm-flood events are becoming increasingly frequent in mountainous valley cities across Asia under global climate change. However, the dynamic evolution and multidimensional resilience effects of cascade disasters triggered by these events remain unclear, limiting effective disaster management. This study focuses on Dongchuan, a typical mountain-valley city in Asia, located at the transition between plateau and mountain regions in China. Based on flood records from 2000 to 2020 and field surveys, rainstorm-flood cascade events and their causal links were extracted. Cascade effects were defined as resilience indicators. A framework combining complex networks, t-SNE dimensionality reduction, and K-Means clustering was used to assess disaster resilience. Clustering quality was evaluated using silhouette coefficients and the Calinski-Harabasz index. Results show: (1) Post-2010, human-impacting events declined by 15 %, while infrastructure-related events rose by 10 %, indicating a shift in vulnerability; (2) Lowland plains, though development-prone, show low resilience due to spatial cascade effects and upstream flood pressure; (3) Under alternating drought-flood climates, resilience patterns became non-stationary, with high-resilience zones in highlands during flood years and in urban cores during droughts. The findings offer valuable guidance for formulating effective disaster prevention policies and resilience enhancement measures in mountainous valley cities across China and Asia.

title: Data-driven time-variant reliability analysis using deep Gaussian processes
abstract: Time-variant reliability analysis (TRA) is critical for assessing the dynamic risk of engineering systems under evolving conditions, such as material degradation and random external forces. However, conventional methods often assume that the statistical properties of all stochastic inputs are precisely known. In practice, these properties must be inferred from limited and often non-stationary measured data, introducing significant epistemic uncertainty. This paper presents a comprehensive, data-driven TRA framework designed to address this challenge. The proposed method integrates multivariate kernel density estimation (KDE) with bootstrapping to non-parametrically model correlated random variables and their epistemic uncertainty. Simultaneously, it employs deep Gaussian processes (DGP) as a probabilistic model for complex, non-stationary random processes, where the epistemic uncertainty is quantified through latent functions. A key contribution of this framework is its ability to systematically quantify and propagate the epistemic uncertainty from input modeling to the reliability prediction, yielding the full probability distribution of the reliability. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through numerical studies by comparing its performance with existing methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides accurate probabilistic predictions, particularly in scenarios with complex non-stationarity and sparse data, thereby enabling more informed risk assessment and decision-making.

title: Predicting initial accident states in hazardous chemical road transportation: A causal and interpretable machine learning approach
abstract: Transporting hazardous chemicals by road involves a high risk of accidents. However, predicting the initial accident state and identifying key influencing factors remain difficult, especially when accident data are limited. To address this problem, this study develops an accident state prediction framework that combines causal inference and machine learning. A random forest model with inverse probability weighting (RF-IPW) is proposed to account for causal effects among accident-related factors. Text-based case reports of hazardous chemical road transportation accidents from 2017 to 2023 are used to extract the causal structure and construct the training dataset. Inverse probability weighting is applied during model training to reduce confounding bias. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method is then used to interpret the model and assess the contribution of each factor. The results show that the proposed RF-IPW model performs well on small-sample datasets after causal effects are considered. Driver state and vehicle condition are identified as the most influential factors affecting the initial accident state. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating causal analysis and interpretability into accident prediction models and support improved risk management in hazardous chemical road transportation.

title: Spatial-temporal graph hybrid neural network for remaining useful life prediction of aero-engines
abstract: Effectively fusing multi-sensor data to improve the accuracy of remaining useful life (RUL) predictions for aero-engines is a critical challenge in prognostics and health management (PHM). The complex operating conditions and variability of sensor signals make it difficult for prediction models to extract key features that reflect equipment degradation trends. Additionally, the sequential network structure can lead to confusion and loss of degradation information, thereby hindering the improvement of prediction accuracy. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for predicting the RUL of hybrid networks based on Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) and Graph Transformer. Effective fusion of multi-sensor information is achieved by constructing spatial-temporal graphs. This method integrates the spatial dependence existing in the data by combining the structural characteristics of aero engines, and enhances the temporal correlation by constructing a local spatial-temporal graph across time steps and a decay matrix based on time distance. Additionally, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network is used to extract node features. Through a parallel architecture combining GCN and Graph Transformer, spatio-temporal features are extracted from multiple perspectives within the spatio-temporal dimension. This approach constructs spatio-temporal representations that incorporate spatial-temporal correlations, thereby enhancing the model's ability to extract spatio-temporal features. Finally, the effectiveness of this method was verified using NASA's C-MAPSS and N-CMAPSS datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that this method exhibits excellent predictive performance.

title: Reliable building inventory imputation for regional-scale risk assessment: An uncertainty-guided framework using spatially-enhanced Transformers
abstract: Regional-scale risk assessments require complete building inventories, yet missing data is a pervasive problem that undermines exposure models and their downstream risk analysis. This study addresses how to impute missing building attributes by explicitly modeling spatial dependencies in a scalable and expressive manner, while simultaneously quantifying the epistemic uncertainty from imputation, moving beyond the limitations of deterministic point estimates. We propose a novel framework that leverages a spatially-aware Feature Tokenization Transformer to impute missing values, then quantifies imputation uncertainty using Monte Carlo Dropout, and progressively refines estimates in an iterative process. On large-scale datasets from San Francisco, our proposed method consistently and significantly reduces imputation error, in some cases nearly halving it over the best performing baseline. It enhances the reliability of regional urban imputation tasks, enabling robust and confident decision-making.

title: A novel deep learning framework for fault propagation analysis in nonlinear and dynamic processes
abstract: In industrial production processes, fault propagation analysis is essential for performing targeted maintenance on malfunctions. Fault propagation analysis for nonlinear and dynamic industrial processes is challenging due to a lack of prior knowledge and the complex correlations between variables. This paper proposes a novel fault propagation analysis method based on a deep learning architecture, which includes two steps: fault localization and causal inference. Firstly, a window-level reconstruction-based contribution method is proposed for fault localization. Specifically, a GRU autoencoder is established to identify and extract sliding data windows containing fault points. Subsequently, the framework of GRU autoencoder is integrated into window-level reconstruction-based contribution analysis to achieve fault localization through aggregate analysis of all faulty windows. When conducting causal inference for fault variables, this paper proposes an adversarial learning-based method for dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) structure learning, which adopts a bi-level optimization framework. This adversarial optimization not only enables accurate modeling of DBNs but also allows for a keen perception of acyclicity in the DBN network. Case studies demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in both fault localization and causal inference for fault variables within nonlinear and dynamic processes.

title: Dynamic forward–inverse prediction of excavations using mobilisable strength design and multi-receptive field convolutional neural network
abstract: Reliable and accurate prediction of retaining wall deflections is critical to the safe design and construction of excavations. The mobilisable strength design (MSD) method, which incorporates soil stress–strain relationships derived from element tests, has attracted considerable attention due to its improved capability in representing soil behaviour more realistically than conventional constitutive models, thereby providing a more reliable framework for the simultaneous prediction of soil deformation and wall equilibrium. However, the effects of spatial variability and sampling disturbance are rarely considered in the determination of soil parameters from laboratory tests, which may lead to noticeable prediction errors in wall deflections when using MSD. This research develops a dynamic approximation optimisation framework integrating MSD and a multi-receptive field convolutional neural network (MRFN) is developed for predicting the deflections of retaining walls in multi-stage excavations. Within this framework, soil parameters are progressively updated based on the measured wall deflections from the preceding excavation stage, thereby reducing the uncertainty associated with soil properties. The proposed method is validated using a well-recorded excavation case, and the results demonstrate that the coupled MSD–MRFN framework can significantly enhance the reliability of wall deflection prediction. This study provides a practical path for improving the accuracy and reliability of geotechnical design through the integration of artificial intelligence.

title: Intelligent early-warning quality control for electromagnets based on long short-term memory network with Bayesian optimisation and exponentially weighted moving average chart
abstract: The quality of electromagnet products is crucial for the smooth operation of mechanical equipment. However, the manufacturing of electromagnet products generates vast amounts of data, which means that real-time monitoring of product quality and ensuring its adherence to standards are challenging. Consequently, traditional quality-control processes for electromagnet product manufacturing lack real-time feedback on quality. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a novel and intelligent early-warning quality control method for an electromagnet manufacturing process. First, a framework for intelligent early-warning quality control is introduced. Second, an intelligent early-warning quality control algorithm is developed. This algorithm integrates a bidirectional long short-term memory network based on a Bayesian optimisation algorithm (BOA-BiLSTM) and an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) control chart method. Third, the implementation process of the early-warning quality control method is analysed using a round-tube electromagnet applied in an electromagnetic trip device. Finally, the practical feasibility of the early-warning quality control method is verified using a dataset of electromagnet product quality. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of the BOA-BiLSTM-EWMA method for early-warning quality control in an electromagnet manufacturing process.

title: Scalable sparse co-Kriging for multi-fidelity data fusion: An application to aerodynamics
abstract: Multi-fidelity Kriging surrogate modeling combines data of varying accuracy, such as experimental tests and numerical simulations, to improve predictive performance. Autoregressive models are commonly used to capture correlations across fidelity levels, offering interpretability compared to purely data-driven approaches. However, existing frameworks often suffer from high computational costs or rely on restrictive assumptions, such as requiring nested designs of experiments (DoEs). In an engineering context, the latter assumption implies that experimental tests must be conducted at the same input conditions as those used in numerical simulations. This requirement cannot always be met due to safety constraints in tests, which limit flexibility in data acquisition. In this work, we revisit the multi-fidelity Kriging approach and introduce a generalized co-Kriging framework that jointly models multiple fidelity levels through a correlation structure based on the autoregressive model. To ensure scalability, we extend sparse approximation techniques to the multi-fidelity setting, maintaining the efficiency of classical sparse Kriging while improving accuracy. We evaluate our framework on both nested and non-nested DoEs. On a large-scale multi-fidelity aerodynamic dataset that combines wind tunnel experiments with CFD simulations, the percentage of standardized residuals falling outside the confidence intervals is reduced by approximately 75% compared to standard sparse Kriging, highlighting the benefit of incorporating multi-fidelity information in complex engineering applications.

title: Optimization of continuous condition-based maintenance for multi-component equipment clusters based on multi-agent incremental reinforcement learning
abstract: The optimization of maintenance decisions for multi-component equipment clusters faces significant challenges in dynamic incremental environments. These challenges include catastrophic forgetting when maintenance environments change, inefficient adaptation to evolving degradation patterns, and difficulties in coordinating spare parts allocation across multiple devices. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Dynamic Incremental Multi-agent Adaptive Reinforcement Learning (DIMA-RL) method based on the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient approach. The method introduces incremental maintenance task environment detection and dynamic adaptive expansion of policy networks. By employing shared parameter extraction layers and isolated task head storage, DIMA-RL prevents interference between policy parameters of old maintenance task environments and new ones, enabling efficient continuous learning in new maintenance environments. Through knowledge distillation techniques, DIMA-RL maintains the model’s decision-making capability in previous maintenance task environments. Finally, to validate our method, different maintenance task environments are set up using the continuous condition-based maintenance decision optimization for port rail-mounted container gantry crane equipment clusters as an example. Experimental results demonstrate that DIMA-RL achieves an average forgetting degree of only 0.71% across all observed task environments while maintaining lower comprehensive continuous maintenance costs than all baselines, showing a 54.83% reduction compared to the Original method.

title: Large language models and AI agents in disaster-resilient infrastructure: concepts, applications, pathways, and challenges
abstract: This paper presents a systematic framework for integrating large language models (LLMs) and AI agents into disaster-resilient infrastructure research. By examining seven key task domains—knowledge anchoring, prediction, assessment, intelligent design and simulation, data augmentation, embodied intelligence, and decision support—we show how LLMs and AI agents can reshape traditional disaster-resilience workflows through enhanced multimodal perception, long-horizon reasoning, cross-stage coordination, and automated task execution. Two representative case studies further demonstrate the feasibility of this paradigm: (1) a multimodal building-damage assessment system capable of city-scale semantic reasoning and transparent diagnostic interpretation, and (2) a LangGraph-based reasoning agent for automated seismic resilience assessment and recovery decision-making of infrastructure systems. These cases highlight the potential of LLMs and AI agents to bridge fragmented data sources, orchestrate multi-stage analytical workflows, and support high-impact resilience applications. Despite these advances, key challenges remain, including data scarcity, reliability and consistency issues, deployment constraints, and ethical or security concerns. Addressing these limitations is essential for developing trustworthy, efficient, and scalable intelligent disaster-prevention systems. Overall, this work establishes a unified cognitive–action paradigm that offers forward-looking pathways for the next generation of intelligent and resilient infrastructure technologies.

title: AI-augmented modeling of post-fire soil hydraulic conductivity across environmental gradients for geohazard assessment
abstract: Wildfires substantially alter soil hydraulic and mechanical properties, reshaping infiltration dynamics and increasing susceptibility to rainfall-triggered geohazards such as debris flows and landslides. A key challenge is the scarcity of paired pre- and post-wildfire soil hydraulic conductivity measurements across vegetation types, soil textures, and burn severities. The main objective of this study is to use generative AI algorithms, together with a curated dataset of measured pre- and post-fire soil hydraulic properties, to augment sparse observations and produce realistic synthetic conductivity pairs across diverse environmental gradients. A curated cross-site dataset of 46 paired conductivity measurements was compiled, and six tabular generators, Gaussian Copula, GAN, VAE, Copula+GAN, VAE+GAN, and a Mixture of Experts (MoE), were trained to produce synthetic conductivity tables conditioned on soil, vegetation, and burn severity. Model performance was evaluated using distributional fidelity metrics, rare-group behavior, memorization diagnostics, and Train-on-Synthetic/Test-on-Real (TSTR) utility. Scale effects were also assessed by varying synthetic sample sizes, and synthetic conductivity contrasts were propagated through a slope stability model to evaluate downstream geotechnical implications. Results show that VAE, VAE+GAN, and MoE provide the strongest balance of fidelity and predictive utility (normalized MAE within 5 to 10% of the real-data baseline) while maintaining low memorization risk (MI ≈ 0.40 to 0.52, versus >0.8 for copula-based baselines). Synthetic datasets enlarged to approximately three to six times the real sample size stabilize dependence structures and improve downstream accuracy. In slope-stability propagation, GAN and MoE most closely reproduced reference factor-of-safety distributions, whereas VAE slightly smoothed lower tails.

title: A low-altitude emergency event grade prediction model integrating attention mechanism and spatio-temporal graph neural network
abstract: Low-altitude safety serves as a critical safeguard for the development of low-altitude economic activities, yet traditional early warning methods struggle to effectively address the complex spatiotemporal dynamic correlations during emergencies. This paper proposes a Low-altitude Emergency Level Prediction Model (GSTA-Net) that integrates attention mechanisms with spatiotemporal graph neural networks. By constructing an adaptive spatial domain graph that combines physical constraints with semantic associations, and designing a gated fusion mechanism incorporating dual spatial and temporal attention, the model achieves precise localization and efficient representation of dynamic spatiotemporal risk patterns. Experiments on an independently developed low-altitude safety dataset demonstrate that the model significantly outperforms mainstream spatiotemporal prediction models in key metrics such as macro-average F1 score and high-level event detection rate. The visualization of attention weights aligns closely with domain experts' analytical logic, showcasing excellent predictive accuracy and decision-making interpretability. This study provides an effective approach for building precise and reliable intelligent early warning systems for low-altitude operations.

title: A review on prognostics and health management applications with federated learning for advanced engineering systems
abstract: Modern engineering systems are increasingly complex and interconnected, making their health management and operational reliability more challenging. Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) enables condition monitoring, fault diagnosis, and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, yet conventional centralized approaches face regulatory barriers, privacy risks, and difficulty in modelling heterogeneous sensor data, while incurring high communication costs at the edge. Federated Learning (FL) offers a decentralized and privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative model training without raw data sharing. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of PHM technologies, FL methodologies, and their integration for distributed, privacy-sensitive industrial environments. We first survey advances in physics-based, data-driven, and hybrid prognostic methods, together with intelligent maintenance and condition-based decision strategies, critically evaluating their adaptability under heterogeneous, resource-constrained settings. We then classify FL approaches by data distribution, network architecture, and participant type, and assess their applicability to PHM tasks through quantitative comparison of privacy-preserving techniques and lightweight deployment strategies. Building on this, we establish a structured mapping between PHM challenges and FL mechanisms, analyse applications in RUL prediction, fault diagnosis, and health monitoring, and identify unresolved gaps. The review concludes with a forward-looking roadmap covering domain-adaptive FL algorithms, resource-efficient edge architectures, and verifiable privacy mechanisms, as well as integration with emerging technologies such as large language models and digital twins. By bridging methodological advances with industrial deployment realities, this work offers actionable guidance for developing scalable, secure, and high-performance PHM solutions in the Industrial Internet of Things era.

title: Causal-enhanced machine learning framework for long-term wind power probabilistic forecasting
abstract: Various and uncertain meteorological factors are the primary reason that makes long-term wind power forecasting formidable, which significantly constraints the reliability and economic viability of wind power. Evaluating the causal relationships between meteorological factors and wind power generation is a promising approach to addressing this issue. Therefore, we propose a novel day-ahead wind power forecasting framework that fuses a directed acyclic graph (DAG)–graph neural network (GNN) causal analysis model a data-driven long-term autoregressive model (autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA)–long short-term memory (LSTM)) and weather condition recognition model based on Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) algorithm to identify main meteorological features with influential causal effect on wind power then quantify uncertainty and perform time series wind power forecasting. An incremental learning strategy is employed to update and calibrate the prediction model continuously. The proposed framework is validated against real-world meteorological and wind power generation data from a wind farm in China. The experimental results demonstrate that this framework effectively captures the inherent uncertainty in long-term wind power forecasting, achieves high probabilistic forecasting performance, and exhibits high prediction accuracy.

title: Multi-sensor spatial and multiscale temporal transformer guided by frequency-domain attention for aeroengine remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for aeroengine prognostics and health management. However, standard Transformer-based models struggle to capture multiscale temporal dynamics and cross-sensor dependencies in aeroengine sensors. Moreover, time-domain scaled dot-product attention does not exploit the degradation characteristics of onboard sensor series or the low-rank structure evident in the frequency domain. We propose Multi-sensor Spatial and Multiscale Temporal Transformer guided by Frequency-Domain Attention (MSMT-FDA), which couples a dual-branch encoder-encompassing multiscale temporal cues and multi-sensor spatial correlations-with frequency-domain low-rank distance attention, leveraging spectral low-rank priors of engine degradation signals. On C-MAPSS (FD001-FD004) and DS02 of N-CMAPSS, our method attains state-of-the-art performance and remains robust across flight regimes, enabling predictive maintenance.

title: Convolutional attention channel factorization mixing network-based state of health estimation for lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Accurately estimating the state of health (SOH) is critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, the performance of existing methods is often compromised by redundant information present in monitoring data. To address this issue, we propose a novel method for SOH estimation based on a convolutional attention channel factorization mixing network (CACFMN). This method consists of a feature extraction module, several channel factorization mixture and temporal processing (CFMTP) modules, and an estimator module. Specifically, a dual-branch convolutional attention module is established to adaptively capture health characteristics from the charging data of LIBs. Furthermore, the CFMTP module is designed to reduce redundancy among the various channels of these characteristics. Subsequently, the estimator module is developed to estimate the SOH of LIBs. Finally, the proposed method was validated using three battery datasets that employed distinct materials and charging-discharging strategies. The experimental results indicate that the designed CFMTP module effectively reduces redundant information across channels, thereby enhancing the accuracy and generalizability of SOH estimation.

title: Joint condition-based maintenance and production of manufacturing systems under flexible decision timing using deep reinforcement learning
abstract: In manufacturing systems, deterioration increases the risk of unmet demand due to reduced product quality and increased downtime. To sustain high productivity and effectively meet demand, efficient coordination between maintenance and production decisions is essential. However, conventional policies typically do not adjust production decisions in response to system deterioration, which can lead to decreased productivity and service levels. This paper proposes a novel and well-motivated framework for the joint decision-making of maintenance and production in parallel manufacturing systems, formulated as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP). Specifically, we incorporate flexible decision timing that allows real-time adjustments to production speeds whenever system deterioration occurs, in order to maintain a high demand fulfillment rate. To solve the resulting large-scale decision-making problem, characterized by a high-dimensional information space encompassing system condition, inventory, demand, and maintenance status, we apply a deep reinforcement learning algorithm: heterogeneous-agent proximal policy optimization (HAPPO). Numerical discussion shows that the proposed method, which derives the joint policy with flexible decision timing and production speed control using HAPPO, outperforms three alternative methods. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that flexible production speed control not only increases total rewards but also improves demand fulfillment. The proposed joint decision-making framework offers a practical and effective solution for deteriorating systems, contributing to the development of more resilient and adaptive manufacturing operations.

title: Spatiotemporal causal modeling of cascading failures in power systems
abstract: • A spatiotemporal causal model is proposed for cascading failure analysis. • A novel counterfactual method performs robust root cause analysis of cascades. • Causal metrics guide more efficient grid hardening than traditional methods. • Causal metrics identify critical components for robust system monitoring. The interconnected nature of modern power grids makes them susceptible to cascading failures, complex events that can trigger widespread blackouts. Data-driven analysis of these events is often limited by an undue on statistical correlation, which hinders model explainability and prevents true root cause analysis. This paper proposes a spatiotemporal causal inference framework that learns the underlying cause-and-effect mechanisms of failure propagation from historical data. The proposed Structural Causal Model enables forward-looking prediction, backward-looking root cause analysis via counterfactuals, and guides grid reinforcement through causal metrics. Results on standard literature test cases validate the framework’s effectiveness. The model achieves high prediction accuracy (84.29%), outperforming several benchmarks, and correctly identifies the initial failure in over 70% of scenarios. Furthermore, a hardening strategy guided by causal metrics is shown to be significantly more efficient than traditional approaches, requiring less than half the number of reinforced components to achieve a comparable level of system reliability. The proposed framework offers a robust, explainable, and actionable methodology for understanding and mitigating cascading failures.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven framework for predicting cascading failure paths in power grids
abstract: As evidenced by large-scale blackouts with severe economic impacts, cascading failures remain a critical challenge that demands intelligent methods to detect hidden propagation paths before they escalate. This work proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework that encompasses codified data generation, methodical model comparison, meticulous hyperparameter optimization, and holistic performance evaluation for propagation paths prediction. Using training data generated under diverse operating conditions for power systems, including IEEE 39, 89, 118 and 300-bus models, this study investigates the performance of decision tree, logistic regression (LogR), k-nearest neighbor, support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) in predicting cascading failure paths, alongside a comparative analysis with the influence model and graph neural networks using graph-level and branch-level accuracy metrics and efficiency metrics, as well as a proposed composite reliability index. To further improve model performance, Bayesian optimization is applied for hyperparameters tuning of the AI methods. Comprehensive numerical experiments are performed, revealing that MLP, SVM, and LogR consistently achieve robust performance while the other models exhibit vulnerabilities under moderate load scaling conditions. The proposed framework can support industry stakeholders in selecting and deploying suitable AI methods for cascading failure prediction in real-world power grid applications.

title: Towards intelligent safety assessment under blast loading: A large language model-powered multi-agent framework
abstract: Reliable and timely safety assessment under blast loading constitutes a critical, expertise-driven challenge, requiring the accurate evaluation of damage effects on specific targets under prescribed conditions. Despite advances in related fields, such as ammunition theory and vulnerability analysis, fully reliable and intelligent safety assessment systems are still in their fancy. This study proposes a novel framework that integrates large language model (LLM) reasoning with multi-agent coordination, featuring domain expertise embedded in customized safety assessment tools, which eliminates the dependency on large-scale training datasets. Experiments across diverse LLM scales, query complexities, and target conditions demonstrate the excellent stability and adaptability of the proposed framework to autonomously complete complex tasks without human intervention. An empirical investigation of system-level target safety assessment substantiates the necessity of an agentic design framework, as the standalone LLM fails to produce correct results even despite employing detailed chain-of-thought reasoning. Complementary evidence from a case study on component-level targets further underscores the importance of the multi-agent architecture. Specifically, the simplified dual-agent configuration struggles to effectively handle more complex task demands. This study highlights the potential of combining artificial intelligence with traditional methodologies, offering a promising pathway for advancing safety assessment and its engineering applications.

title: Adaptive and robust scheduling subject to machine degradation and breakdowns in networked multi-factory systems via hierarchical multi-head deep reinforcement learning
abstract: In equipment-intensive manufacturing, machine degradation and breakdowns threaten system robustness and production continuity, while multi-layer couplings and dynamic collaboration in mass-customized networked multi-factory systems exacerbate these challenges. This study addresses the robust scheduling problem for networked multi-factory systems with machine degradation and breakdowns under mass customization (MC-NMFRS-MDB) and proposes a hierarchical multi-head deep reinforcement learning (HMH-DRL) approach. The problem is formulated as a multi-Markov decision process with a high-dimensional state space capturing degradation and breakdown dynamics, a dual-layer action space addressing coupled subproblems, and a multi-head reward balancing performance and robustness. A hierarchical multi-head policy architecture enables coordinated decision-making and multi-objective optimization. The training process employs prioritized experience replay to improve learning efficiency, nonlinear clipping to stabilize policy updates, and a retraining mechanism for continual adaptation. Numerical results indicate that HMH-DRL reliably converges, improving scheduling performance and robustness by over 10.59% and 10.98%, respectively, compared with four DRL methods, three metaheuristic algorithms, and one reliability-driven heuristic, confirming its effectiveness in complex and dynamic scenarios.

title: A deep-learning-based approach for temporal transportation network dismantling
abstract: Accurately assessing the importance of individual nodes at different time for maintaining the efficiency of temporal transportation networks is an important challenging problem. It is for the first time that this issue has been formulated as a temporal network dismantling (ND) problem, which aims to identify the minimal set of nodes with time information whose disruption can rapidly degrade temporal network efficiency. This paper proposes a deep-learning-based network dismantling framework for its solution. Specifically, a directed acyclic graph representation is used to capture the continuous topological changes in a temporal network. Then, our framework employs multi-head graph attention networks to learn latent higher-order features by aggregating different temporal features of nodes and their neighbors, and incorporates the shortcut connections technique to mitigate the vanishing gradient problem. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world networks demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms baselines and exhibits significant robustness. Furthermore, an early warning signal indicator is adopted to quantify the dismantling risk of temporal networks. Our approach offers a practical tool for identifying critical nodes in temporal transportation networks, thereby assisting stakeholders in enhancing robustness of transportation services.

title: An adaptive sparse Bayesian neural network-informed incremental prediction method for remaining useful life of rolling bearings
abstract: The high prediction accuracy of deep neural network (DNN) relies on abundant high-quality training data. However, the remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of bearings is confronted with scarce failure data and poor degradation consistency, which severely restrict the generalization ability of DNN models and the reliability of prediction results. To address this issue, this paper proposes an adaptive sparse Bayesian neural network-informed incremental prediction method for rolling element bearings. Specifically, a temporal cascaded Bayesian neural network framework is designed through the collaborative coupling of Bayesian probabilistic modeling and temporal cascaded network structure, thereby enabling quantitative characterization of prediction uncertainty while capturing the dynamic degradation trend of bearings. Aiming at the widespread issue of high complexity of BNN models, an importance-guided parameter preservation mechanism is constructed to retain parameters encoding professional knowledge while pruning redundant network components for explicit model lightweighting. At the incremental prediction stage, a stage-adaptive correlation alignment strategy is developed to dynamically learn the intrinsic knowledge correlations between different stages, thus alleviating degradation inconsistency issues and improving the model’s generalization and robustness. Experimental results on two test benches indicate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and excellent generalization ability, while comparative experiments with several state-of-the-art methods further validate its robustness and superiority.

title: Interpretable deep learning framework for urban bus traffic safety situation forecast
abstract: Accurate forecasting of urban bus traffic safety is essential for transportation authorities to plan traffic systems, formulate safety policies, and promote public transit use. However, the current understanding of the evolutionary patterns and correlation mechanisms of bus traffic safety with operation-related factors remains limited.​ Thus, this study proposes an Adaptive Three-Stage Temporal Feature Forecasting(ATS-TFF) framework. Taking a mountainous Chinese city as an example, it forecasts the trend of urban bus traffic safety situation (BTSS) and analyzes the relationships between BTSS and multiple influencing factors.​ The results reveal at the feature level, factors such as the mean number of downstream bus stops in the road sections, the mean number of tunnels allowing lane changes along the routes, and the maximum temperature all have substantial effects on BTSS. Temporally, BTSS most significantly affects itself five days later. At the interaction level, the mean number of downstream bus stops in the passed road sections four days prior has the most important impacts on BTSS. ​Overall, the proposed ATS-TFF framework and findings provide data-driven support for proactive bus system safety management, advancing the shift from reactive control to forward-looking, targeted intervention strategies.

title: Data-driven co-design of power distribution networks for resilience enhancement through graph neural network aided performance estimation
abstract: To enhance the resilience of critical infrastructures, a co-design optimization framework is developed for the design of the distribution network and its recovery scheduling. Since network representations are distinct from conventional numerical data, the framework needs to be tailored to overcome unique challenges. Due to the networks being represented as graphs rather than numerical values, derivative-free optimization is the most suitable option. In a random search, the neighborhood must be defined considering the graph data structure. In this study, a surrogate model that can estimate the resilience of the network system is built using a deep-learning-based graph neural network (GNN) to reduce the computational burden during a derivative-free optimization algorithm. Network vulnerabilities are identified using centrality measures from graph theory, where the total demand loss is quantified with sequential component removals to represent resilience loss. Integrating the design optimization to the recovery problem defined as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model, the proposed framework can find the optimum solution for network design and recovery resource scheduling. To prove the efficacy of the proposed GNN-based co-design framework, it was applied for a power system benchmark, where the results demonstrated the practicality of the framework.

title: Active learning Kriging with spherical low-discrepancy sampling and gradient refinement for efficient reliability analysis of geotechnical systems
abstract: Reliability analysis of geotechnical systems often requires numerous high-fidelity simulations to evaluate complex limit state functions (LSFs), resulting in prohibitive computational cost. Traditional surrogate-based approaches, such as active learning Kriging with Monte Carlo simulation (AK-MCS), often suffer from local clustering of background samples and inefficient exploration of the failure domain, especially in high-dimensional problems. To address these limitations, an enhanced active learning Kriging framework, termed AK-SLDS, is developed. The method integrates a spherical low-discrepancy sampling (SLDS) scheme with a gradient-refined learning strategy to improve the global representativeness of background samples and the local accuracy of surrogate updates. The performance of AK-SLDS is verified through five numerical examples, including two benchmark problems and three engineering applications. The two benchmark problems demonstrate the method’s accuracy and efficiency for low- to medium-dimensional reliability analyses. The engineering examples, involving the bearing capacity of a shallow footing and two slope stability problems, confirm its robustness for strongly nonlinear and high-dimensional geotechnical systems. Results show that AK-SLDS produces failure probability estimates in close agreement with MCS while requiring substantially fewer true LSF evaluations compared with conventional active learning approaches. The method thus provides an efficient and reliable framework for conducting reliability analysis in geotechnical systems.

title: Active learning with dynamic exploitation-exploration balance for aircraft engine remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for aircraft engines using deep learning is often hindered by the scarcity of labeled run-to-failure data. Active learning (AL) addresses this by selecting the most informative samples for labeling, but traditional methods often use fixed criteria and fail to properly balance the exploitation-exploration trade-off. This paper proposes a novel AL framework that dynamically manages this balance. We utilize a Bayesian hybrid deep learning model to quantify prognostic uncertainty. Based on this, we develop a dual-criteria acquisition function, which integrates uncertainty and diversity by using a feedback mechanism to dynamically adjust their balance. To mitigate redundancy in batch queries, we also introduce a greedy selection algorithm to promote intra-batch diversity. Validation on the C-MAPSS and PHM08 benchmark datasets demonstrates that our framework achieves high RUL prediction accuracy with significantly fewer labeled samples than the compared AL strategies.

title: A data-driven framework for failure probability prediction of water supply pipelines: Integrating feature selection and homogeneous grouping
abstract: Accurate prediction of water supply pipeline failure probability over a future period is vital for risk prevention. Within the prediction period, pipeline failures are typically modeled as a Poisson process. Nonetheless, the scarcity and poor quality of historical failure data necessitate homogeneous grouping to estimate average failure rates. A key challenge in this process is determining how to select appropriate features for grouping, as it directly affects prediction accuracy. This study proposes a data-driven framework integrating feature selection and homogeneous grouping to improve failure probability prediction. First, failure observation samples for a specific time period are generated based on the pipeline’s failure records. A layered feature selection strategy combining filter and wrapper methods is designed to balance selection efficiency with model performance. Filter methods are used to identify candidate feature subsets based on correlation with failure rates. These subsets are then used for grouping, resulting in multiple failure probability labeled datasets. For each, prediction models are developed using Artificial Neural Network and Support Vector Regression. The optimal feature subset and corresponding model are determined by comparing predictive performance. The framework’s effectiveness is validated using a case study of water supply pipelines in the central area of Shanghai, China.

title: A Bayesian uncertainty-guided transfer learning method for trustworthy fault diagnosis of rotating components
abstract: The overall reliability and safety of mission-critical equipment, such as aero-engines, largely depend on the health of their rotating parts. Therefore, trustworthy fault diagnosis is essential for achieving reliability-centered health management. Existing methods face several challenges under cross-working conditions, including computational redundancy, a high risk of negative transfer, and a lack of awareness of uncertainty. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel trustworthy fault diagnosis method based on transfer learning. More specifically, first, a domain-shared feature encoder that fuses sparse self-attention and a deep CNN is designed to extract local and global features. Second, a Bayesian classifier based on variational inference is constructed and combined with Monte Carlo sampling to quantify epistemic uncertainty. Then, a domain alignment mechanism combining explicit and implicit discrepancy measures is introduced. Meanwhile, the uncertainty is mapped via an exponential decay function into adaptive weights that guide domain alignment, thereby prioritizing the transfer of high-confidence samples and suppressing unreliable ones. Finally, the experimental results on the gear dataset show that the proposed method achieved the highest accuracy rate of 99.11% in three transfer tasks. Moreover, among the correct predictions, 91.84% fall within the low-uncertainty region, while all misclassifications are flagged as high-uncertainty. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can provide trustworthy, uncertainty-aware diagnostics to enhance the reliability and safety of complex mechanical systems.

title: A correlation-aligned proxy-learning framework for few-shot prediction of battery remaining useful life
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for quantifying battery operational safety and longevity, yet the deployment of machine learning techniques is often constrained by a widespread deficiency of high-quality labelled degradation data. To address this challenge, we propose a correlation-aligned proxy-learning framework that establishes a principled bridge between scarce RUL labels and opportunistic ageing cues. The framework employs a bilateral-branch neural network to explicitly disentangle initial manufacturing variability from in-use degradation dynamics, ensuring robust feature extraction across heterogeneous cells. By recasting a class of differential incremental capacity (ΔIC)-based descriptors as proxy labels, the method leverages their strong intra-cell and through-life correlation with RUL to transform the under-determined few-shot regression problem into a consistency-matching task. This strategy effectively constrains the model’s learning manifold, enabling the exploitation of non-ideal indicators from routine charging events while mitigating the risk of overfitting. Validated across diverse battery chemistries and cycling temperatures, the framework significantly outperforms conventional semi-supervised baselines, delivering more than a 50% improvement in prediction accuracy under extreme few-shot regimes.

title: Virtual sensing by grey-box modelling within an importance sampling Monte Carlo dynamic event tree framework for risk monitoring of small modular reactors
abstract: Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) integrate advanced safety features. However, the compactness of their core design renders it difficult to position measurement devices, for operation and risk monitoring. To address this issue, we develop a Grey-Box (GB) modelling framework that ensembles White-Box (WB) physics-based and Black-Box (BB) data-driven models to enable virtual sensing of in-core safety-critical variables. The BB model is trained with condition monitoring data to perform multi-step ahead estimation of measurable variables; the estimates are fed to a physics-based WB model to estimate the non-measurable variables. The GB model developed is embedded within a risk monitoring module that builds on an Importance Sampling Monte Carlo Dynamic Event Tree (IS-MCDET) to provide the risk profile of the SMR. The method is tested on the Small Modular Dual Fluid Reactor (SMDFR), a new-generation SMR whose developed GB model for risk monitoring consists in a zero-dimensional Thermal Hydraulic (TH) WB model and a Bi-directional Long-Short Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) BB model. The developed GB model is shown to comply with the regulatory requirements and explainable response to support risk-informed decision making.
keywords: Importance sampling Monte Carlo dynamic event tree (IS-MCDET)

title: Development of urban fire risk index based on fire damage weighting methodologies and AI analysis of meteorological factors
abstract: As urban density increases, the development of reliable quantitative indicators for fire risk assessment becomes essential for disaster management. However, existing studies have tended to rely on single weighting methods without validating their suitability for predictive modeling based on meteorological conditions. This study constructed fire risk indices using three distinct methodologies: principal component analysis (PCA) for statistical objectivity, analytic hierarchy process (AHP) for expert judgment, and value of statistical life (VSL) for economic valuation. Using ten years of fire and meteorological data from Busan, risk grades were classified using K-Means clustering, and predictive models were developed via a Random Forest (RF) classifier based on four key meteorological variables (average temperature, maximum wind speed, effective humidity, and sea-level pressure). Comparative analysis revealed that the AHP and VSL models, which placed excessive weight on fatalities, showed low correlation with meteorological conditions and poor predictive performance for high-risk events (recall < 0.20). In contrast, the PCA-based index effectively captured the physical mechanisms of fire spread under low temperature, dry, and high-pressure conditions. The PCA model achieved a precision and recall of 0.99 in classifying high-risk grades. While AHP and VSL are useful for post-event impact assessment, this study demonstrated that the PCA-based index is the most scientifically valid and reliable measure for a meteorology-based predictive early warning system.

title: Optimizing fault tree traversal order for efficient minimal cut set generation: A lightweight graph neural network approach
abstract: Although the downward method is widely used in fault tree analysis, the critical impact of sibling node traversal order on computational efficiency has received insufficient attention. Current approaches rely on either fixed heuristic rules or random selection, resulting in unstable computational performance. To address this challenge, we introduce graph neural networks to intelligently optimize node traversal order. We construct a comprehensive dataset that maps graph structures and node orderings to computational costs, and propose a novel two-stage training framework: a cost prediction network that evaluates ordering quality, followed by a ranking generator guided by predicted costs. Experimental evaluation on industrial fault trees demonstrates that our GNN-based approach consistently identifies efficient traversal strategies, achieving 1.5–40 × speedups over conventional methods and competitive performance against established solvers. By transforming the discrete combinatorial optimization problem into a learnable task, this work provides a new perspective for optimizing topological traversal in minimal cut set analysis.

title: Energy-saving optimization of train speed Profile based on online Policy deep reinforcement learning algorithm under emergency conditions
abstract: In the domain of energy-efficient train-speed-profile optimization, off-policy reinforcement-learning (RL) algorithms and their variants have long dominated the academic landscape. Such approaches typically rely on an experience-replay buffer to reuse historical samples, yet they suffer from low training efficiency, poor numerical stability, and insufficient real-time responsiveness—limitations that become critical in complex metro systems or under emergency conditions. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose an on-policy RL framework termed the Energy-Saving Maximization Advantage Distribution (ES-MAD) algorithm. ES-MAD abandons the replay buffer and instead employs dual policy networks (new vs. old): data collected by the newly explored policy are immediately leveraged to update the old policy, thereby markedly improving sample efficiency. In addition, a normalized-and-scaled advantage function is introduced to reduce variance, which significantly enhances model stability in highly dynamic or emergency scenarios. Finally, a multi-objective, self-adaptive reward mechanism is designed that seamlessly integrates energy efficiency, punctuality, ride comfort, and stopping accuracy; this reward structure requires no re-tuning when the system switches between normal and emergency operating modes. Experimental validation on the Yizhuang metro line demonstrates that ES-MAD exhibits strong robustness and generalization capability under regular service, sudden schedule changes, and multi-interval comprehensive tests. Compared with state-of-the-art off-policy deep RL baselines, ES-MAD achieves 24 % and 26 % additional energy-saving under normal and emergency conditions, respectively.

title: Batch active learning for reliability-based model validation
abstract: In engineering, quantifying the deviation between model prediction and reality is crucial, particularly when simulation or empirical models are used in safety-critical applications or for product release. Model validation aims to quantify this discrepancy by comparing model predictions to experimental results. However, conducting physical experiments for validation is often costly and time-consuming. Active learning strategies can mitigate this problem by reducing the data needed to assess model accuracy. In practice, these strategies must account for experimental uncertainties, such as material variability. This work proposes an active learning framework for model validation focused on efficiently identifying the limit state between valid and invalid model regions under such conditions. Therefore, we introduce a decision-theoretical basis from which we derive two novel misclassification-based acquisition functions for mean-based and quantile-based validation. Furthermore, the framework is extended to the batch setting, allowing multiple points to be proposed for evaluation while considering nonlinear constraints of the input space. The proposed method is compared to alternative approaches for several analytical and engineering problems. Finally, the validation of a temperature model for an electric motor demonstrates the efficiency of the method in a complex scenario.

title: A k-GNN Wiener process interactive RUL prognosis method for stochastic degrading devices monitored by related multiple sensors
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for making proactive decisions regarding the health management activities of degrading devices, thereby effectively ensuring safe, reliable, and economic operations. For degrading devices monitored by multiple sensors, hybrid prognosis methods combining statistical-model-based and deep-learning-based approaches, have become popular in the field of prognostics and health management. However, existing studies based on open-loop model architectures, tend to overlook the correlations and complementary relationships among multiple sensors, leading to a reduction in prediction accuracy. Therefore, this paper presents a novel data-model integrative prognosis framework incorporating high-order graph neural networks (GNNs) and Wiener process (WP). Specifically, a k-order GNN (k-GNN) capturing the high-order interaction information among different sensors is utilized to construct a composite health index (CHI). Subsequently, the time-varying stochastics within the CHI is depicted through a WP. By joint learning parameters of the k-GNN with those of the WP, a closed-loop framework is established to improve the matching degree between the constructed CHI and the WP-based degradation models. Both experimental results on simulated datasets including C-MAPSS and N-CMAPSS and real-world case study results on milling cutter dataset demonstrate that the proposed k-GNN-WP model achieves a substantial improvement in RUL prediction accuracy.

title: Towards AI-Driven smart maintenance of computed tomography equipment: From health indicator design to transferable remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Failures of Computed Tomography (CT) equipment can disrupt hospital operations and compromise patient safety. However, research on Predictive Maintenance (PdM) for such systems remains limited. The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) provides a practical foundation by enabling real-time acquisition of high-dimensional operational data. This study proposes a deep learning framework for predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of CT equipment. First, a physics-guided Health Indicator (HI) is defined as the deviation between the observed current and the predicted nominal current of the X-ray tube filament. Second, a CT-specific degradation path identification module that combines operational state filtering with adaptive signal fusion to extract smooth, physically consistent trends is proposed. Third, a bidirectional LSTM sequence-to-sequence model, combined with cross-equipment transfer learning and uncertainty quantification, is developed for RUL prediction under heterogeneous work states and across different equipment. The framework is validated on real-world IoMT-collected X-ray tube filament datasets from multiple hospitals and CT equipment. The proposed framework achieves prediction errors of 0.3, 3.0, and 2.3 days with error rates of 0.23%, 2.33%, and 1.78%, respectively, outperforming classic and recent strong baselines in temporal alignment and generalization. These results demonstrate the potential of IoMT-enabled PdM to support maintenance decision-making, clinical workflow optimization, and downtime minimization.

title: EPAL: An exponential-penalty based active-learning function for adaptive Kriging models in structural reliability analysis
abstract: Accurate estimation of structural failure probability in engineering systems is frequently limited by the high computational cost of evaluating complex performance functions. This paper introduces an exponential-penalty based active-learning (EPAL) function for adaptive refinement of Kriging models in reliability analysis. The EPAL formulation integrates the Kriging predictive variance with a normalized distance measure relative to the predicted limit-state surface through an exponential decay term. This functional form dynamically suppresses the selection of new samples in regions of low predictive uncertainty or those far from the failure boundary. The inherent resistance to sample clustering ensures a balanced sampling strategy that simultaneously explores regions of high uncertainty and refines the vicinity of the failure boundary. A key feature of this design is that the EPAL function is mathematically simple, parameter-free, and continuously differentiable. By removing the need for empirical tuning parameters or auxiliary distance thresholds, the method reduces subjective bias and computational redundancy. Numerical results from multiple benchmark problems confirm that the proposed method provides accurate failure probability with high computational efficiency. Its effective performance in both engineering applications and problems with small failure events further demonstrates its suitability for reliability analysis involving expensive simulations.

title: A data-efficient surrogate-based structural reliability approach using a firefly-optimized deep neural network: Application to hang-off drilling riser evacuations
abstract: Reliability assessment of offshore structures subjected to nonlinear hydrodynamic-structural interactions requires uncertainty propagation that is statistically consistent with the full response space. However, fully coupled finite-element (FE) simulations are too computationally expensive for Monte Carlo (MC) analysis, limiting their applicability in nonlinear structural reliability. This study develops a data-efficient structural reliability methodology that integrates nonlinear FE simulations, a firefly-optimized deep neural network (FA-DNN) surrogate model, and MC uncertainty propagation into a unified framework. The methodological innovation lies in the FA-DNN model, where a multi-objective firefly optimization strategy adaptively tunes hyperparameters to improve learning stability, prevent overfitting under limited FE data, and accurately reproduce nonlinear response behavior required for reliability evaluation. Trained on a small FE-generated dataset, the FA-DNN achieves R² values above 0.996 and reduces prediction errors by over 90% compared with ANN and baseline DNN models, enabling fast and statistically consistent MC-based estimation of failure probability. Application to a deepwater riser system in hang-off evacuation serves as a verification example, demonstrating that the methodology yields reliability-informed operational limits with negligible computational cost. The framework is general and transferable, offering an efficient surrogate-enhanced pathway for nonlinear reliability assessment of offshore and other complex structures under stochastic loading.

title: The prediction of limit wheel profile using geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural networks
abstract: Wheel profile prediction is critical to the maintenance of high-speed electric multiple units. This study proposes a geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural network for high-accuracy prediction of worn wheel profiles. A vehicle–track dynamic simulation model is further employed to determine whether predicted worn profiles exceed the limit and to estimate the time-dependent reliability associated with profile degradation. The proposed approach is evaluated via quantitative and qualitative comparisons with a conventional wheelset wear prediction method. Results indicate that the geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural network improves wheel wear prediction accuracy. In addition, the simulation-based prediction is more conservative, and the wear range observed in service is wider than that obtained from simulation. Wear patterns of wheels within the same wheelset also show strong correlations. Moreover, wheel diameter affects wear behaviour, including the wear degradation rate, equivalent conicity, the vehicle critical speed, and the Sperling index. Hence, Maintenance scheduling should therefore account for wheel diameter effects to ensure robust performance and durability.

title: Bayesian deep learning framework for pesticide transport modeling with uncertainty quantification
abstract: Pesticide transport and transformation in soil pose potential threats to ecological environments and human health, while traditional numerical simulation methods exhibit high computational costs and difficulty in accurately quantifying prediction uncertainty. A Bayesian deep learning framework is developed for pesticide transport modeling, integrating uncertainty quantification, interpretability analysis, and risk assessment. Surrogate models including deterministic, MC Dropout, and Deep Ensemble architectures are constructed based on 447,300 COMSOL simulation data points. The Deep Ensemble model achieves the optimal balance between prediction accuracy (R2>0.96) and uncertainty quantification, with calibration errors of 0.0350–0.0467. SHAP analysis reveals the dominant role of second-layer soil hydraulic parameters, which simultaneously constitute the primary sources of model uncertainty. Spatiotemporal uncertainty analysis shows that the mean prediction uncertainty decreases from 0.21 to 0.05 within 14 days and remains stable at 0.04–0.08 over the full 365-day period.The risk assessment framework reveals that contamination risk escalates from a mean probability of 0.476 (t=2 days) to 0.837 (t=28 days) with 72.1% of the domain classified as very high risk, and the early warning system indicates that the alert and emergency thresholds are triggered at 2.0 and 4.0 days, respectively. Climate change impacts are quantified through 10 scenario analyses: warming reduces the near-surface mean concentration by 18.8% via the Q10 effect, while precipitation changes affect transport through the source concentration (c0) and infiltration forcing (Hp0) pathways, with the c0 pathway dominating most exposure metrics. Under extreme drought conditions, the high-concentration area of aldicarb sulfoxide reaches 20.0–57.2%, far exceeding baseline levels. The framework provides a comprehensive approach to uncertainty-aware pesticide transport prediction, with future extensions needed for three-dimensional heterogeneous systems and multi-pesticide synergistic effects.

title: Adaptive parameter estimation-based neural sliding mode control for uncertain singular Markovian jump systems against actuator attacks
abstract: This article primarily focuses on tackling the challenge of adaptive parameter estimation-based neural sliding mode control for singular Markovian jump systems under actuator attacks The singular Markovian jump system exhibits adaptive uncertain parameters and inaccessible states. Furthermore, due to vulnerable control signals during transmission, the actuator may receive compromised commands from malicious attacks. To mitigate the effects stemming from actuator attacks, neural network (NN)-based strategy is employed to approximate and evaluate the fraudulent information introduced by adversaries. Subsequently, the online estimation of uncertain system parameters is conducted by leveraging the derived adaptive law. Meanwhile, a newly designed sliding mode observer is integrated into the system to evaluate the unobservable states, thereby significantly enhancing the comprehensiveness of system state monitoring. An innovative adaptive neural sliding mode control strategy is presented, which is designed to ensure that both the estimated states and their corresponding errors are capable of converging to the sliding manifolds. Simultaneously, this strategy guarantees the stochastic admissibility of the uncertain singular Markovian jump systems. Ultimately, the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method are demonstrated through empirical research on the direct-current (DC) motor and the Quarter-Car active suspension (QCAS) model.

title: Graph-based deep reinforcement learning for adaptive and scalable post-earthquake bridge network restoration
abstract: Rapid restoration of bridge networks following earthquake events is crucial to ensuring transportation continuity, reducing economic disruption, and supporting emergency response. This study proposes a novel graph-based deep reinforcement learning framework (GNN-DRL) that synergistically integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), and a Top-k action filtering mechanism, to enable adaptive and scalable post-earthquake bridge network repair scheduling under resource constraints. The proposed approach captures network topology and dynamic bridge states to prioritize sequential bridge repair decisions across a restoration planning horizon. The GNN-DRL decision policy is evaluated on several case-study bridge networks with varying sizes and is compared to other restoration policies including ranking-based, mixed-integer linear programming, and DRL-only policies. Sensitivity analyses are carried out to examine the effect of the Top-k filtering mechanism on balancing bridges network resilience and computational complexity, for practical real-time deployment. Results show that the proposed GNN-DRL policy consistently achieves faster and more effective restoration as well as higher final functionality throughout the planning horizon, demonstrating the potential of AI-guided infrastructure restoration to enhance disaster resilience in complex transportation systems. The framework offers a practical balance of resilience, scalability, and computational efficiency suitable for rapid post-earthquake restoration decision support.

title: Efficient time-variant reliability analysis through parallel adaptive Gaussian process modeling based on look-ahead sampling strategy
abstract: During the full life cycle of engineering products, structural performance inevitably degrades over time and is affected by uncertainties. Time-variant reliability analysis (TRA) plays a crucial role in ensuring safety and evaluating service life. However, accurately characterizing the time-variant failure probability within limited computational resources remains a challenging task. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel method termed parallel time-variant stepwise error reduction (PTSER) for efficient TRA within the single-loop Gaussian process framework. The core lies in constructing a look-ahead learning function to explicitly account for the impact of current sampling decisions on the future model accuracy. Subsequently, parallel sampling is achieved by combining probability-weighted importance and correlation-based diversity control.
