The spatial sparsity of damage indices (defined as the structural parameter change) and loads is adopted as priors in the Bayesian framework. The Expectation-Maximum (EM) algorithm is used to iteratively estimate the most probable values of the damage indices, unknown force time history, measurement noise, and other variance parameters. A modified Metropolis-Hastings (MH) algorithm is developed to jointly generate posterior samples of structural parameters and loads for the expectation calculation in the EM algorithm. Upon convergence, some hyperparameters approach infinity and the associated damage indices and forces become zero, resulting in the sparsity of the identified damage indices and loads. Consequently, the damage indices and input forces are located and quantified simultaneously, and the full-field structural responses are sequentially reconstructed with suppressed uncertainties. The proposed method is verified by a numerical simply-supported beam, a laboratory-tested three-story frame model, and a three-span continuous bridge model. Results demonstrate that the proposed sparse Bayesian technique can accurately identify the damage indices, loads, and responses simultaneously, even when the load position is unknown.

title: A double-loop adaptive Kriging-based robust design optimization method with aleatory and epistemic uncertainty
abstract: Robust design optimization under aleatory and epistemic uncertainty still remains several key issues, such as lack of a unified quantitative robustness measure, suffering from huge computational burden and in need for proper searching strategy, etc. To remedy these, a novel adaptive Kriging-based robust design optimization method with aleatory and epistemic uncertainty is proposed. Based on the unified MC-based simulation technique for both aleatory and epistemic uncertainty, a decision model for robustness measure is built to comprehensively characterize the nominal expectation, the variation due to epistemic uncertainty alone, and the mixed variation due to both epistemic and aleatory uncertainty. To solve the decision model, a double-loop adaptive Kriging-based method is proposed, which can ensure a balance of optimality and robustness with limited calculations of the real deterministic objective. The inner-loop Kriging is locally updated at each training sample of the outer-loop one to ensure accuracy of the minimization and maximization at each focal element of the deterministic objective, while the outer-loop Kriging is deeply coupled into each simulation level of the subset simulation optimization to quickly converge to the optimum without much loss of accuracy. A toy example is used to illustrate the performance of the proposed methodology, engineering applicability of which is further tested by three real engineering examples.

title: Adaptive Kriging‑assisted enhanced sparrow search with augmented‑Lagrangian first-order reliability method for highly efficient structural reliability analysis
abstract: Uncertainty information exists widely throughout the life cycle of engineering products. Efficient reliability analysis methods are essential to solve complex reliability problems considering multi-source uncertain information. In this study, a hybrid method combining the Active Kriging (AK) model with Enhanced Sparrow Search Optimization (AK-ESSO) is proposed to enhance the performance of classical First-Order Reliability Method (FORM). In the first stage, ESSO’s ability to search for reliability indicators is enhanced through adaptive global search and random local search strategies. In the second stage, the augmented Lagrangian penalty function in FORM is used to enhance the accuracy of the optimization model used to approximate reliability indicators in ESSO. In the third stage, the novel hybrid AK strategy considering global and local accuracy is proposed to enhance the computational efficiency in the limit state assessment process. By combining these three strategies, AK-ESSO enhances the robustness and global performance of FORM in searching for reliability indicators. Using eight numerical and three applicable engineering problems, the AK-ESSO frameworks applied in FORM are compared to the classical FORM algorithm, popular FORM-based metaheuristic algorithms, and hybrid Kriging-based metaheuristic algorithms. The results indicate that AK - ESSO offers significant advantages in efficiency, and in terms of computational accuracy, the augmented Lagrangian optimization probabilistic model provides significant advantages for AK - ESSO, as well as global convergence in terms of robustness.

title: Variational inference for hierarchical Bayesian learning framework for model updating with non-stationary prediction errors
abstract: Quantification of model uncertainties are essential for ensuring the credibility of numerical models in robust structural response prediction and reliability assessment. Probabilistic model updating provides an effective way to achieve this purpose. Among these methods, the hierarchical Bayesian modeling (HBM) framework has been widely recognized as a powerful tool for jointly estimating the uncertainty of model parameters and prediction errors, thereby enabling a comprehensive quantification of model uncertainties. Typically, Gaussian white noise (GWN) is used as the probabilistic model for prediction errors, but this assumption fails to capture their non-stationary characteristics. To overcome this limitation, a new HBM framework is developed, which replaces GWN with a Gaussian process (GP) model. An orthogonal expansion is utilized to approximate the GP model as the summation of orthogonal functions with independent Gaussian coefficients for efficient error representation. The use of GP introduces a coupling relationship between the model parameters and the Gaussian coefficients, which makes it impossible to directly infer their joint posterior distribution. To resolve this issue, variational inference is employed. Specifically, the mean field assumption is utilized to decouple the parameters into independent sets, and the variational distributions of each set are sequentially inferred. To ensure consistency across these distributions, an iterative procedure is designed, where the evidence lower bound serves as the convergence index. Through iterative sequential inference, the optimal variational distributions for each parameter set are obtained, and their product approximates the joint posterior distribution. Additionally, the model class selection approach is utilized to determine the optimal number of orthogonal terms for simulating prediction errors, striking a balance of simulation accuracy and complexity. With the estimated uncertainties of model parameters and the GP model of prediction errors, the uncertainty of the output quantity of interest can be predicted. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is validated using two examples in structural dynamics.

title: Incomplete cost-sensitive collaborative learning-based manufacturing quality predictive modeling method under heterogeneous sensing
abstract: The manufacturing quality of the product plays a vital role in the reliability of the complex equipment and the overall system safety. Accurately predicting manufacturing quality helps promptly detect abnormal products and shorten production time. Nevertheless, the multi-source heterogeneous sensor data on the manufacturing systems will unavoidably result in incomplete data, thereby affecting the accuracy of the predictive model. In addition, the imbalanced data in quality labels can deceive conventional models to obtain inexact predictive boundaries, leading to missed detection of abnormal manufacturing products. In this study, an new incomplete cost-sensitive collaborative learning-based model is proposed for manufacturing quality prediction. Specifically, an improved probabilistic principal component analysis-based incomplete learning module is first designed to supplement heterogeneous data information. After that, an elaborated cost-sensitive quality predictive model is developed to handle the imbalanced quality labels. Finally, an evolutionary collaborative learning strategy is appended to enhance predictive performance via collaboratively optimizing the incomplete and cost-sensitive learning modules. Application case studies of actual wheel bearing component and valve manufacturing plants demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves higher accuracy in manufacturing quality abnormal prediction.

title: Ensemble multimodal fusing learning for geological identification in tunnel construction
abstract: This paper proposes an ensemble multimodal deep learning approach to identify the geological conditions in shield tunnel engineering. The proposed approach improves the Swin Transformer architecture, building a multimodal model with soil images and tunnel boring machine (TBM) parameters as input. The Dempster Shafer theory is used for information fusion to develop the Ensemble Swin-Transformer-MLP (ESwin-T-M), which accurately identifies geological conditions for tunnel shield projects. In addition, the Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-Cam) and the Model-Agnostic Permutation Feature Importance (MAPFI) are used to perform model interpretation analysis. The Circle Line Phase 6 C885 Tunnel Project in Singapore is used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results indicate that: (1) The proposed ensemble multimodal fusing network identifies geological conditions with a high F1-Score of 0.9746 in 5-fold cross-validation. (2) The recognition accuracy of the ensemble multimodal fusion network is superior to that of the single modality models and the basic models. (3) The ensemble fusing approach outperforms the approaches utilizing soil images or TBM parameters separately in terms of robustness and anti-interference ability. The novelty of this research lies in the development of an integrated detection method for multimodal information, which overcomes the trustworthy limitations of traditional single-data method and provides technical support for the precise and reliable identification of geological conditions in tunnel engineering.

title: An online prediction method for airplane landing risk in extremely windy conditions based on stream learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of landing risk during extremely windy conditions is vital to ensuring flight safety. However, most existing methods rely on pre-trained single-risk models, which often have poor prediction accuracy under extremely windy conditions such as strong winds. This study proposes an online multi-risk prediction method for airplane landing during extremely windy conditions, leveraging a streaming Bi-LSTM-Transformer (BLT) architecture. First, data preprocessing is performed to ensure the high-quality input for analysis. A comprehensive multi-risk assessment framework is then developed to evaluate the potential landing risks, utilizing the processed data. Subsequently, time-series modeling is conducted using a Bi-LSTM network. To improve the models’ global time-series modeling ability, a Transformer component is integrated into the Bi-LSTM output, forming the BLT model. Finally, stream learning is introduced to maintain predictive performance under extremely windy conditions. Using real-time flight data streams, the Stream BLT model applies eligibility traces and a dynamic learning rate to enable continuous, adaptive learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method accurately predicts airplane landing risks under extremely windy conditions, particularly when wind speeds exceed 33knots. The model achieves an average relative error of approximately 0.01–0.07 and a prediction latency of under 30 ms, offering efficient, reliable real-time airplane landing risk assessment.

title: Multi-level adaptive risk control: synergistic maintenance-termination optimization with online parameter learning
abstract: Catastrophic functional disruptions of degrading systems during task executions usually incur severe safety repercussions and substantial losses, necessitating prompt risk mitigation strategies. It is therefore of paramount significance to develop distinct risk intervention levels following refined degradation evaluations. This study establishes a collaborative self-adaptive optimization problem of routine maintenance and task termination decisions for heterogeneous degrading systems. A Bayesian learning methodology is employed to continuously update the unknown degradation rate utilizing equidistantly sampled data; leveraging such updates constitutes an adaptive multi-level risk control policy employing age-state-dependent thresholds to select between (a) operational continuation, (b) routine maintenance partially restoring degradation at a severity-dependent cost, or (c) terminate the task instantly for overhaul. In order to minimize the total expense encompassing maintenance expenditures, task failure penalties, and termination losses, we identify several key findings into the optimality of the multi-level control policy, showcasing that the policy is representable as a monotonic threshold policy relative to degradation progression. Implementation on shipboard phased-array radar drivers confirms the framework’s operational viability and demonstrates substantial advantages over conventional strategies in risk loss prevention and task success promotion.

title: Adaptive portfolio optimization-based metamodel method for the multi-armed bandit problem of learning function in slope reliability analysis
abstract: Adaptive metamodels using single learning functions fail to consistently maintain the high accuracy or efficiency in calculating failure probabilities of slopes under all scenarios (e.g., natural vs. reservoir slopes) due to the No Free Lunch theorem. It poses a challenge in the adaptive selection of the optimal function under high-dimensional random field domains. To this end, we consider the selection problem as a multi-armed bandit problem, and thus propose a portfolio optimization-based adaptive polynomial-chaos Kriging (POPCK) method that dynamically balances exploration and exploitation of six distinct learning functions, thereby adaptively selecting better functions based on their historical performance. This adaptive selection could be performed under high-dimensional variables by incorporating Karhunen–Loève expansion and sliced inverse regression techniques into POPCK. The feasibility of the proposed method is demonstrated through four classic examples (involving natural, four soil layers, rainfall infiltration, and water level drawdown conditions). Results show that the proposed method exhibits good robustness for all examples, high accuracy (ranking 1st) and computational efficiency (ranking 2nd), whereas the performance of PCKs using the single learning functions fluctuates greatly. This method effectively mitigates the randomness of learning function selection, which is valuable for engineers who lack prior knowledge of optimal learning functions.

title: An efficient reliability assessment framework for complex mechanism wear degradation based on probabilistic space decomposition kriging model
abstract: Operational wear in complex mechanical systems with joint clearances, driven by nonlinear dynamic behavior, leads to functional degradation and accelerated failure. While critical, the influence of vibration on wear progression is often overlooked in existing studies, and efficiently assessing the reliability of high-fidelity simulation models remains a significant challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a reliability assessment framework for wear degradation (PSDK-WDR). First, we develop a non-uniform wear prediction model that integrates a nonlinear dynamic model with the Archard wear model. This model innovatively updates the wear coefficient using parameters derived from real-time vibration signal energy dissipation. Furthermore, for efficient reliability analysis, we introduce a Monte Carlo simulation method based on a Probability Space Decomposition Kriging model (PSDK-MCS). This method decomposes high-dimensional random variables into subsets via Probabilistic Space Decomposition (PSD) and constructs parallel Kriging sub-models for each subset to accelerate assessments. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed wear model and the PSDK-WDR framework are validated through case studies on crank-slider and flapping-wing mechanisms. This work provides a theoretical basis for understanding wear evolution and efficiently evaluating reliability degradation in complex mechanisms.

title: Nested adaptive Kriging-based reliability analysis and computational resource allocation for complex systems
abstract: Efficient reliability analysis of complex engineering systems faces significant challenges due to the integration of multiple subproblems, multidisciplinary coupling, high-dimensional characteristics, and resource incompatibility. These systems are often decomposed into multiple cascading subsystems, which enables concurrent analysis to manage this complexity. Surrogate-based techniques are widely utilized to alleviate the computational burden associated with time-consuming simulations. This study proposes a nested adaptive Kriging-based method for the reliability analysis of complex systems by integrating system decomposition with adaptive surrogate-based methods. The proposed method operates within a multilayer framework and proceeds in two stages, namely, a sequential updating stage and a resource allocation stage. In the first stage, an efficient nested reliability-oriented acquisition function is developed to guide model updating, and its closed-form expression is derived. In the second stage, a cost-effectiveness strategy that accounts for both simulation costs and modeling costs is introduced to determine which model combinations should be updated at each iteration. Finally, the proposed method is validated to be superior to the benchmark method and strategy through two mathematical examples and two practical applications.

title: Domain knowledge-enhanced dual-stream graph joint learning network for aeroengine remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Prediction methods integrating domain knowledge with deep learning show great promise for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of aeroengines. Nevertheless, neglecting the decoupling modeling of multi-level domain knowledge such as component-level physical topology and parameter-level essential dependencies has resulted in insufficient and incorrect utilization of valuable degradation information, limiting the further improvement of prediction accuracy and stability. Therefore, a novel domain knowledge-enhanced dual-stream graph joint learning network (DK-DGJLN) is proposed. First, the physical essential dependencies among components and sensor parameters are extracted through in-depth analysis of aeroengine’s overall structure and working characteristics. Then, a component-level static graph is built to capture physical topology with high fidelity, while a parameter-level dynamic graph is constructed to model dynamic dependencies and degradation evolution. Their decoupling modeling enables faithful embedding of multi-level domain knowledge. Finally, a DGJLN is designed to extract rich and complementary spatial-temporal degradation features from both graphs, with a self-attention-based feature alignment module aggregating them for accurate RUL prediction. Extensive comparative experiments on the C-MAPSS dataset against 19 SOTA methods demonstrate that DK-DGJLN significantly improves prediction performance, especially on FD002 and FD004, where the RMSE values of 12.93 and 13.57 are markedly lower than those of the best comparative methods.

title: Multi-granularity learning-based intelligent decision-making method for equipment operation and maintenance on large-scale knowledge graphs
abstract: Effective equipment operation and maintenance (O&M) is crucial for productivity and safety; however, traditional manual decision-making methods are hindered by long cycles and inconsistent accuracy. This paper introduces MulKGR, an intelligent decision-making model designed for large-scale O&M knowledge graphs, addressing challenges such as insufficient multi-level fault association and low decision-making efficiency. The model extracts multi-granularity subgraphs from the O&M knowledge graph, incorporating equipment status, failure modes, and environmental factors to construct relational paths that enhance decision-making. MulKGR then employs a graph convolutional network (GCN) to jointly encode problem text and relational paths, generating word embeddings and calculating similarity scores, thereby optimizing computational efficiency through subgraph pruning. Finally, the pruned subgraphs are processed by a reasoning decision module that integrates GCN with long- and short-term memory networks for dynamic learning, enabling accurate reasoning and answer generation. Experimental results from a new energy vehicle production plant show that MulKGR significantly improves decision-making, achieving an F1 score of 65.88 %, a Hits@1 score of 62.5 %, and reducing decision-making time by 5.69 %. These results demonstrate the model's effectiveness in intelligent decision-making for equipment O&M.

title: Graph learning with variational graph structural information bottleneck for multi-sensor machinery remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Existing graph learning-based remaining useful life (RUL) prediction approaches typically rely on predefined structural priors or fixed constraints to optimize graph topologies. Such priors are often crafted for specific signal modalities and thus exhibit limited generality, restricting their ability to model the complex and heterogeneous interdependencies inherent in multi-sensor signals. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a graph learning framework with a variational graph structural information bottleneck (GL-VGSIB) for multi-sensor machinery RUL prediction. The proposed GL-VGSIB establishes an information-theoretic graph structure learning paradigm that adaptively discovers degradation-relevant graph representations by balancing discriminability and compressibility. In contrast to prior GNN-based RUL frameworks that depend on static structural priors, the variational bottleneck mechanism in GL-VGSIB infers a probabilistic distribution over graph structures, enabling the model to preserve essential task-relevant dependencies while suppressing redundant or spurious connections. The framework integrates a multi-scale convolutional encoder with positional encoding to enhance spatio-temporal feature extraction and employs a reparameterization mechanism to facilitate differentiable stochastic graph sampling. Experimental results on two multi-sensor equipment datasets show that GL-VGSIB achieves a 2.9%-14.8% reduction in prediction error relative to state-of-the-art baselines, thereby demonstrating its effectiveness to multi-sensor machinery RUL prediction.

title: Active Kriging-based uniform importance sampling with rejection control for highly efficient and accurate structural reliability analysis
abstract: Developing highly efficient and accurate structural reliability analysis for high computational cost and low failure probability problems is critical for engineering application. In this paper, a novel active learning strategy coupling with weight control and adaptive distance control is proposed for Kriging-based uniform importance sampling. The rejection control is introduced to improve the efficiency of reliability analysis. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through numerical cases and three aerospace engineering applications, which showed that the proposed strategy could reduce both the cost of performance function evaluations and surrogate model calls. The repeated results validated that the proposed method is efficient, accurate, and robust, proving its capability to address real-world engineering challenges.

title: Risk predictive deduction and propagation chain mining for URT emergencies based on interpretable ensemble learning: A new approach to in-time safety management
abstract: To enhance the emergency response capability of Urban Rail Transit (URT), this paper proposes an in-time safety management approach based on explanatory ensemble learning and key risk chain mining. Firstly, an innovative in-time safety management framework is designed. On this basis, historical incident data from Beijing Metro in recent years is used to identify risk causation and impact range. A dynamic risk assessment and predictive deduction method based on explanatory Stacking ensemble learning model is designed. It incorporates Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) for sample balanced and Optuna for optimal hyperparameter tuning of both base and meta models, achieving superior prediction accuracy for risk impact levels. Then, SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) is employed to identify key risk causes and quantify their influence on prediction results. Finally, an improved W-Apriori algorithm is employed to mine the complex associations within key risk propagation chains, thereby providing targeted emergency response strategies. To demonstrate the approach, this paper presents a simulation case based on real operational emergency data and indicate that the proposed model achieves 95.83% accuracy, outperforming traditional machine learning methods across five performance metrics and exhibit superiority to promote a shift in URT safety management from traditional reactive response to proactive prevention and in-time intervention.

title: Physics-constrained causal structure learning for root cause analysis in nuclear system monitoring
abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) is important for identifying the initiating cause of faults and analyzing fault propagation paths in nuclear systems. However, robust RCA in nuclear accident monitoring remains challenging because it depends on reliable identification of causal relationships among monitoring variables, which is difficult under complex system coupling and limited-sample conditions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a physics-constrained causal structure learning method for RCA in nuclear accident monitoring. First, a simplified physical model of the nuclear system is constructed to extract a priori causal knowledge among key monitoring variables. Second, the causal relationships among different variables are learned by a score-based causal structure learning method under the guidance of the extracted physical constraints. In this process, physically infeasible edges are excluded and the admissible parent sets are restricted before score optimization. Finally, the root cause nodes of faults are identified based on the learned causal graph. The proposed method is validated using two representative accident scenarios generated from a nuclear simulation platform. The results show that the proposed method can improve root-node identification performance, reduce abnormal-edge misidentification, and enhance the robustness of causal structure learning under limited-sample conditions without introducing additional computational burden.

title: Dynamic branch expansion: A hypergraph-augmented adaptive continual learning framework for machine health prognosis under time-varying conditions
abstract: Industrial data streams with dynamic distributions pose more daunting challenges for data-driven machine health monitoring. Continual learning (CL) method has the ability to adapt to newly-collected data and retain partial memory of previous degradation knowledge, while it still sinks into a dilemma of insufficient accumulation for long-term and diverse degradation patterns under complex operating conditions (OCs). This study proposes an adaptive continuous health prognosis framework with dynamic branch expansion (DBE) for absorbing dynamic data streams to predict the remaining useful life of rotating machines under time-varying OCs. Among it, an OC-aware hypergraph topology network is designed to enhance the hypergraph representation, after which hypergraph topology-memorized knowledge buffer is established for optimal replay sampling. On this basis, an adaptive DBE framework is constructed, which self-recognizes the addition of branches with the continuous influx of new data; and it ingeniously integrates multi-branch predictions via branch discriminator logits at inference stage to enhance CL generalization capability. Case studies of multi-stage continuous prognosis are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results indicate that it can gradually enhance the prediction performance with incremental data, and maintain the predictions of old data while fully learning degraded knowledge at new stages.

title: Risk-oriented degradation modeling and maintenance decision support for computed tomography X-ray tubes using mechanism-informed learning
abstract: Accurate estimation of the remaining useful life (RUL) of Computed Tomography (CT) X-ray tubes is essential for maintaining medical service continuity, reducing failure risk, and minimizing unplanned downtime. However, intrinsic degradation patterns are often obscured by heterogeneous operating conditions, such as automatic tube current modulation and voltage optimization. To address this challenge, we propose the Hybrid Affine Gated Fusion Network (HAGF-Net), a deep learning framework tailored for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments. HAGF-Net employs a dual-branch parallel architecture that integrates physical priors with data-driven features. One branch processes Mechanism-driven Indicators (MDIs) derived from filament degradation physics, including cathode degradation rate (CDR) and degradation kinetic increment (DKI), using a Conditioned Operating-Gated Transformer (COG-Transformer) that dynamically modulates attention weights based on discrete operational states. Simultaneously, a raw-signal Branch based on CNN-LSTM modules captures local fluctuations and long-term temporal dependencies from multi-dimensional sensor sequences. The framework was validated on a high-resolution IoMT dataset comprising 10 Philips X-ray tubes from multiple clinical sites across China (2017–2024), covering their entire service lives. HAGF-Net demonstrates high global predictive accuracy (RMSE = 0.07) and precise final-stage performance (MAE ≈ 3.85 days) and 95% prediction intervals close to the nominal coverage across sites. Ablation and comparison studies indicate that incorporating physical MDIs and condition-aware gating mechanisms enhances model’s robustness and responsiveness to complex degradation dynamics. Under simulated unreliable monitoring conditions, the proposed method evaluates model robustness under reduced sampling frequencies, demonstrating stable performance across different levels of data sparsity.

title: Mining of Fault Propagation Mechanisms in Computer Numerical Control Machine Tools via Information Fusion and Association Rules
abstract: Enhancing the reliability of CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machine tools requires precise identification of fault propagation paths. However, existing methods often treat macroscopic topology and microscopic mechanisms in isolation and suffer from biases inherent in single-source data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a reliability-oriented mechanism mining framework integrating information fusion and Association Rule Mining (ARM). First, a game-theoretic weighted Decision Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL)–Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) method is proposed to fuse expert knowledge with failure statistics. This constructs a robust hierarchical topology that mitigates data sparsity. Second, using this topology as a physical constraint, a constraint-based Apriori algorithm is developed. With downtime-centric constraints, it extracts microscopic failure mechanisms from abstract paths. It also overcomes the limitations of traditional algorithms in capturing temporal logic and fault chains. A case study on a five-axis machining center identifies the Electrical System as the most influential subsystem within the identified fault propagation topology and the Automatic Tool Changer (ATC) as the most susceptible unit. The proposed method detects latent High-Impact Low-Probability (HILP) chains and improves Precision, Recall, and F1-score by 2.56 ×, 1.75 ×, and 2.16 × over the traditional algorithm. These results demonstrate improved consistency with the topology-constrained reference patterns for reliability diagnosis of complex electromechanical systems.

title: Positioning Road-level Flood Sensing for Disruption Assessment based on Uncertainties and Bayesian Networks
abstract: Urban flooding severely disrupts road traffic, and assessing these disruptions in a near real-time manner depends on road-level flood sensing that is usually constrained by limited financial and manpower resources. Therefore, positioning a limited number of sensing nodes requires valuing candidate locations. Yet existing strategies value locations mainly by traffic volume or local flood severity rather than disruption, and consider roads in isolation, overlooking how disruption propagates between connected roads. This study builds a double-layered Bayesian network that couples roads through their flood and traffic dependencies. A flood observed at one road then propagates to the inferred traffic disruptions across the connected network. Each candidate location is scored by the Value of Information (VoI) it contributes, combining the magnitude of the revealed traffic disruptions with how far they depart from historical expectation. A greedy algorithm then places sensing nodes where this network-wide value is the greatest. In a New York City expressway case study, the network estimates traffic speeds and the relative levels of disruption, and a few well-placed sensing nodes capture most of the attainable value. The VoI-based positioning achieves higher accumulated value than heuristics based on flood probability, traffic volume, or disruption alone. The framework is expected to help transportation and emergency agencies deploy limited flood-sensing resources where they most improve real-time traffic disruption assessment during urban floods.
